Drizzle with the reserved sausage cooking oil and sprinkle with some of the remaining parsley before serving.
noteCook: If you like spicy heat, consider choosing hot chouriço.
To make it a meal, serve the soup over hot, freshly cooked rice.

recipe.name: Chirper's Sugar Biscuits

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons packed light or dark brown sugar
{=amount1/v} sheet frozen all-butter puff pastry (see Cook's Notes), thawed according to package directions and still cool
{=amount1/v} tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature, plus {=amount2/v} tablespoons melted

instructions: In a medium bowl, combine 2 tablespoons of the granulated sugar and the lemon zest and stir until the sugar is moist and fragrant. Add the brown sugar, cinnamon, cardamom, and salt and stir to mix thoroughly. Set aside 2 tablespoons of the mixture.

Place a sheet of parchment paper on your work surface and evenly sprinkle the remaining 2 tablespoons granulated sugar over it. On the sugared paper, unfold the puff pastry (which should be rectangular) and, if it is less than 15 inches long, place a second parchment sheet over it and use a rolling pin to gently roll it to that length (taking care not to press too hard, which compresses the layers, decreasing their puff when baked). Remove the top parchment sheet. If necessary, using your fingers, gently loosen the long edge of the pastry nearest you from the bottom piece of parchment paper (this will make it easier to begin rolling it with the filling). Evenly spread the room-temperature butter over the pastry and sprinkle the larger quantity of the sugar mixture over the butter, all the way to the edges. Lay a piece of parchment paper over the sugar mixture, gently press down to help the mixture adhere, and remove the parchment.

Starting with the long side that you loosened, gently roll the pastry into a very tight, even, compact cylinder. Pinch the seam along the entire length of the cylinder to seal (it may pop open as the buns bake, which is fine). Slide the cylinder and the parchment sheet it's on onto a large baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate until firm, about 45 minutes.
With a rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F. Coat the cups of a standard muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray, and set aside.

Remove the plastic from the pastry, place the cylinder seam-side down on a cutting board, and, using a serrated knife in a sawing motion, cut the cylinder in half crosswise. Cut each half into sixths and place, cut-side up, in a prepared muffin cup.

Bake the buns until puffed and dark golden brown, about 20 minutes, rotating the muffin tin about halfway through. Remove the buns from the oven and, working quickly, brush with the melted butter and sprinkle each with about ½ teaspoon of the reserved sugar mixture. Let cool for 3 minutes, then carefully remove the buns from the muffin tin while still hot. Let cool on the rack to room temperature (they'll crisp up more as they cool) before serving.
noteCook: The dimensions of puff pastry sheets vary by brand, so depending on which one you use, you may or may not have to roll it to the required length. Regardless, make sure your pastry is completely thawed, so you can unfold it initially, and roll it up with the filling, without it cracking. It should still be cool, though, because warm puff pastry can become sticky. Finally, don't allow the baked buns to cool completely in the muffin tin, or they will stick to the cups.

All that said, don't allow all this information daunt you. The buns are, in fact, easy to form and bake, and easier yet to eat. On that note, they're best within a couple of hours of baking. You can, however, re-crisp them with about a 5-minute stay in a 350°F oven.

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoon plus {=amount2/v} cup Dutch-process cocoa powder
{=amount1/v} cups all-purpose flour, plus more for your work surface and dusting
{=amount1/v} tablespoons ({=amount2/v} stick) unsalted butter, frozen and grated on large holes of grater

ingredients.name: SWEET YAK BUTTER

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons ({=amount2/v} stick) unsalted butter, at room temperature, cut into 8 pieces
{=amount1/v} tablespoons honey, or more, to taste

entries: Kosher salt

instructions.name: Make and glaze the scones:
entries: Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside. In a small bowl, whisk 2 tablespoons of the confectioners' sugar and 1 teaspoon of the cocoa powder and sprinkle it evenly over the prepared baking sheet.

In the bowl of a food processor, pulse the remaining ⅓ cup of cocoa powder, the flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and espresso powder (if using) to combine. Scatter the grated butter over the flour mixture and pulse until the mixture forms a mealy texture with pea-size crumbs, about eight 3-second pulses. Pour this mixture into a large bowl, add the chocolate chips, stir to distribute, and make a well in the center.

In a small bowl, whisk the egg, cream, and 1½ teaspoons of the vanilla until uniform. Add the liquid to the flour mixture and, using a flexible spatula, fold until the mixture looks shaggy and very little dry flour remains at the bottom of the bowl (the dough will be sticky).

Flour a work surface, turn out the dough, sprinkle a little flour over the top, and knead gently just until uniform and cohesive (try to keep the kneading to a minimum). Divide the dough in half, place the two pieces on the prepared baking sheet, and pat them gently into two 6-inch circles, each about ¾ inch thick.

With a chef's knife or bench knife, and flouring the blade between each cut, cut each circle into 6 wedge-shaped pieces, pressing down decisively and firmly, without sawing (a clean cut helps the scones rise). Flour a butter knife, shimmy it under one of the dough pieces, and pull gently to separate it from the rest of the circle by about ½ inch. Repeat with the other pieces to separate them while leaving their circle formation intact. Place the baking sheet in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 500°F.

Lower the oven temperature to 400°F. Bake until the scones are puffed, the edges and tops are set, and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 15 minutes, rotating the baking sheet halfway through. Remove from the oven and cool for about 10 minutes while preparing the glaze.

Meanwhile, set a wire rack on another baking sheet. In a medium bowl, whisk the remaining 1 cup of confectioners' sugar, 1 teaspoon of vanilla, and 2 tablespoons of water until smooth. Dunk the tops of the warm scones into the glaze and place them on the wire rack until cooled and the glaze has set, about 15 minutes.

instructions.name: Make the sweet yak butter:
entries: In a medium bowl, combine the butter, honey, and a tiny pinch of salt. Use a fork to mash them together until thoroughly combined. Adjust the seasoning with additional honey and/or salt, if necessary. Scrape the mixture into a small serving dish and serve at room temperature with the scones immediately or within about 2 hours.

recipe.name: Chopforest

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup Kalamata olives, pitted and finely chopped
{=amount1/v} medium fennel bulb, trimmed, cored, and thinly sliced, plus about 1½ tablespoons chopped fronds
{=amount1/v} medium scallions, trimmed; whites thinly sliced and greens cut into ½-inch lengths

instructions: In a colander or large strainer set over a medium bowl, toss the cabbage with 2 teaspoons salt. Let the cabbage rest until slightly wilted, at least 1 hour or up to 4 hours. Rinse the cabbage well under very cold running water, drain thoroughly, and dry very well with a clean kitchen towel or paper towels. Scrape the cabbage into a large bowl and fluff it with your fingers (it can be covered and refrigerated for up to 3 days).

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine the olives, vinegar, lemon zest, garlic, and ½ teaspoon salt; season with pepper; and whisk to incorporate. While whisking vigorously, add the olive oil in a slow, steady stream to combine and emulsify into a dressing.

Add the cabbage, fennel bulb, scallions, and parsley to the bowl and toss to combine. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary, and sprinkle with the fennel fronds before serving.
noteCook: You can substitute thinly shaved fresh brussels sprouts for some or all of the cabbage if you'd like. It will decrease the yield a bit, as brussels sprouts leaves are more delicate than cabbage, and they compact more once dressed. If you use shaved brussels sprouts, there's no need to salt and rest them.

recipe.name: Chultan Zombie
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} orange slices, pineapple chunks, and/or maraschino cherries for garnish

instructions: Fill a cocktail shaker about halfway with ice and add the rum, pineapple juice, orange juice, grenadine, lime juice, Cointreau, and bitters. Cover and shake to blend and chill, 30 seconds. Fill two chilled Collins or highball glasses about halfway with ice. Strain half the mixture into each. If using, add 1½ ounces seltzer to each glass and stir gently. Garnish each cocktail as desired and serve at once.
noteCook: If you don't have any Cointreau to add sweetness and flavor, you can substitute 1½ teaspoons superfine sugar to each drink. To make superfine sugar, simply spin regular granulated sugar in the blender or food processor to break down the crystal size, which will allow it to dissolve in liquid more readily.

This is a high-volume drink, and cocktail shakers vary in size; so you may have to prepare the cocktails one at a time. Boston shakers, the type used in most bars, are larger than cobbler shakers with built-in strainers, which are common for home use.

recipe.name: Chultwater
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup fresh passion fruit pulp (see Cook's Note)

instructions: Fill a serving bowl or other large drinking vessel three-quarters of the way full with ice. Add the blue curaçao, dark rum, light rum, falernum, lemon juice, pineapple juice, orange juice, and passion fruit to the bowl and stir to combine. Garnish with mint and basil. Serve at once in rocks glasses.
noteCook: If you can't find fresh passion fruit at your local market, look for frozen passion fruit pulp with seeds.

recipe.name: Cloaks

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks
{=amount1/v} tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small cubes, at room temperature

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Place the potatoes in a large microwave-safe bowl, cover with a microwave-safe lid or plate, and microwave until very tender, about 18 minutes, stirring the potatoes twice during that time. Spread the potatoes on a baking sheet or large plate and let cool until you can handle them, about 5 minutes. Set a potato ricer over the empty bowl and rice the potatoes into it. Add half the butter cubes and stir to incorporate. Add the half-and-half, 2 teaspoons salt, ¾ teaspoon pepper, the nutmeg, and cayenne and stir to incorporate. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary. Add the egg and yolks and baking powder and stir until the mixture is uniform and very smooth. Let cool to room temperature, add the remaining butter cubes, and fold to incorporate.
With a rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 475°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a nonstick baking mat and coat it lightly with nonstick cooking spray.

Scrape the potato mixture into a piping bag fitted with a ½-inch star tip. Hold the filled pastry bag slightly above the prepared baking sheet and apply steady, gentle, downward pressure to pipe a mound roughly 2 inches in diameter and 2 inches high. Work your way out in a tight circular motion, and then back in again to build height. Pipe twenty mounds total, with about 1 inch between them (five rows of four mounds). Lightly coat the mounds with cooking spray.

Bake the cloaks until golden brown, about 14 minutes, rotating the baking sheet about halfway through. Let cool on the baking sheet for 2 minutes, then, using a spatula, transfer to a serving platter. Serve immediately.
noteCook: If you don't have a pastry bag, you can get away with a heavy-duty ziplock freezer bag as a substitute. Snip off about ⅜ inch from a bottom corner and fit the star tip into the hole, pushing it through from inside the bag.

Although you'll sacrifice the crisp ridges created by the star tip, you can use a spoon to shape the mounds into circles or ovals of about the same dimensions as the piped version, and run the tines of a fork over the surface to add texture.

recipe.name: Cocoa Broth

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup unsweetened cocoa powder, preferably Dutch-processed
{=amount1/v} cup packed light brown sugar, or to taste
{=amount1/v} cups espresso or very strong black coffee, hot

instructions: In a saucepan over medium heat, whisk together the cocoa powder, brown sugar, cinnamon, cardamom, salt, and water until smooth. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook, whisking constantly, for about 2 minutes, making sure the whisk gets into the edges of the pan. Whisk in the milk and bring to a simmer (do not boil), whisking frequently, about 10 minutes. Whisk in the vanilla and espresso. Taste and adjust the flavor with additional brown sugar, if desired. Divide among four mugs, add the marshmallow (if using), and serve.

recipe.name: Community Cheeses

ingredients.name: Dippers
entries: Broccoli and/or cauliflower, trimmed and cut into bite-size florets
Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
Roasted or steamed potatoes, cubed
Apples and/or pears, peeled, if desired, cored, and cut into bite-size pieces (toss with a small amount of fresh lemon juice to slow browning)
Ham steak, sautéed until lightly browned, and cut into bite-size pieces
Baguette or other good French bread, cut into bite-size pieces (each with some crust)
Raisin bread or dried fruit-nut bread or rolls, lightly toasted and cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.name: Fondue

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} ounces Gruyère cheese, coarsely grated ({=amount2/v} cups, lightly packed), at room temperature
{=amount1/v} ounces Emmental cheese, coarsely grated ({=amount2/v} cups, lightly packed), at room temperature

entries: Pinch of freshly grated nutmeg (optional)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black or white pepper

instructions: PREPARE THE DIPPERS. Blanch the broccoli or cauliflower in boiling salted water until just tender, about 4 minutes. Drain and transfer to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking. Then drain until dry or blot dry.
MAKE THE FONDUE. In a large bowl, mix the Gruyère and Emmental cheeses and set aside. In a small bowl, whisk ⅓ cup of the wine and the cornstarch to blend, and set aside.

In a heavy saucepan over medium heat, combine the remaining 1⅓ cups of wine and two of the garlic cloves and bring to a simmer. Remove the garlic, whisk the cornstarch mixture to recombine, add it to the pan, and stir constantly, until thickened, 15 to 30 seconds. Stir in the lemon juice.

Adjust the heat to medium-low and add about ½ cup of the cheese, stirring constantly but gently until fully melted. Repeat with the remaining cheeses in ½-cup increments, each time stirring until melted fully before adding more, about 8 minutes. Continue to cook, stirring constantly but gently, until the mixture is smooth and just begins to bubble, about 4 minutes more. Do not allow the mixture to boil; adjust the heat, if necessary. Add the Kirsch, nutmeg (if using), ½ teaspoon salt, and pepper to taste. Stir to combine. Taste and adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary.

Meanwhile, warm a fondue pot with hot water, empty it, and dry it well. Rub the inside of the pot with the remaining garlic clove and pour in the fondue. Set the pot over a heat source, and serve at once with the dippers.
noteCook: There is a lot of variation in the way cheeses melt. To increase your odds of a smooth outcome, use grated cheese at room temperature. Many experts advise using cheeses that are younger than a year old and avoiding those sourced from supermarket deli counters.
Cheeses can differ in saltiness, so season the fondue carefully. Start with ½ teaspoon kosher salt, and taste. If necessary, add more salt by the ¼ teaspoon.

recipe.name: Corn and Lentil Soup

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ounces zucchini, trimmed, quartered lengthwise, and cut into ½-inch pieces (about {=amount2/v} cups)
{=amount1/c} medium garlic cloves, pressed or grated (about {=amount2/v} tablespoons)
{=amount1/v} cups red lentils, rinsed well in a strainer

instructions: In a large, heavy pot over medium-high heat, warm 1½ teaspoons of the oil until shimmering. Add the zucchini and ¼ teaspoon of salt, stir to coat with the oil, spread across the bottom of the pot, and cook, undisturbed, until lightly browned, about 3 minutes. Scrape the zucchini into a large bowl.

Return the pot to medium-high heat, add 1 tablespoon of the oil, and warm it for a moment. Add the corn and ¼ teaspoon of salt, stir to coat with the oil, spread across the bottom of the pot, and cook, undisturbed, until lightly browned, about 3 minutes. Scrape the corn into the bowl with the zucchini.

Return the pot to medium-high heat, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of the oil, and warm it for a moment. Add the onions, bay leaves, and ½ teaspoon of salt and cook, stirring, until the onions are soft and light golden, about 4 minutes. Adjust the heat to medium-low, cover and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions have released their juices, about 3 minutes longer.

Adjust the heat to medium, clear the center of the pot, add the tomato paste, and cook in the clearing, stirring, until sticky and fragrant, about 2 minutes. Stir the paste and onions together. Add the cumin, coriander, cayenne, and garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the broth, 2 cups of water, and tomatoes, adjust the heat to high, and bring to a boil. Add the lentils and ½ teaspoon of salt and stir to mix. Adjust the heat to low, cover, and simmer until the lentils are fully tender and begin to split apart, about 35 minutes, adding the reserved zucchini and corn after about 25 minutes.

Remove and discard the bay leaves. Add pepper to taste, most of the cilantro (reserving a little for garnish), and lime juice, and stir to mix. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt, black pepper, and lime juice as necessary. Ladle into individual bowls, sprinkle with a portion of the remaining cilantro, and serve.
noteCook: Red lentils turn golden and break down when they cook, so this soup's consistency ends up similar to that of a thin split pea soup.
If you're not vegetarian, you can use chicken broth in place of the vegetable broth.

recipe.name: Corned Beef and Cabbage

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ({=amount2/v}-pound) corned beef brisket, flat (or thin) cut, rinsed well and fat trimmed to about a {=amount3/v}-inch-thick layer, if necessary
{=amount1/v} pounds (about {=amount2/v}) small red-skinned or Yukon gold creamer potatoes, scrubbed
{=amount1/v} ({=amount2/v}-pound) small head green cabbage, tough outer leaves removed, cut through the core into {=amount3/v} wedges

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons unsalted butter, softened and cut into small pieces

instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F with a rack in the middle position of the oven.

In a large Dutch oven, combine the garlic, pickling spice, corned beef, onion, carrots, and celery. Add the broth and enough water to just cover the meat and cook, covered, until the corned beef is super-tender (a paring knife should slip easily into the meat), about 4 hours. Transfer the meat to a baking dish; trim and discard the fat, if desired. Strain and reserve the cooking liquid, and discard the solids. Pour about 1 cup of the liquid over the meat, cover the dish tightly with foil, and let rest for about 30 minutes.

Pour the strained cooking liquid into a fat separator or measuring cup and rest until the fat rises to the surface, about 10 minutes. If you are using a fat separator, pour the liquid into another container; if you are using a measuring cup, tilt it and use a wide, shallow soup spoon to skim any fat off the surface and discard it.

Return the liquid to the Dutch oven, add the potatoes, set the pot over medium-high heat, and bring to a simmer. Adjust the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the potatoes just begin to soften, about 8 minutes. Add the cabbage, submerge it in the liquid as best you can (arrange the potatoes among the cabbage wedges), replace the cover, adjust the heat to medium-high, and return to a simmer. Adjust the heat to medium-low and simmer until the potatoes and cabbage are both tender, 10 to 14 minutes more, turning over the cabbage wedges after 6 minutes.

Meanwhile, place the meat on a cutting board, slice it against the grain into thin slices, and set the slices on a large serving platter. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the vegetables to a large bowl and sprinkle them with salt, if necessary, and pepper to taste. Scatter the butter pieces over the vegetables, wait a moment for the butter to begin to melt, and gently turn over the vegetables to distribute the butter. Arrange the potatoes and cabbage around the meat on the platter, sprinkle the parsley over the meat and vegetables, and serve with vinegar on the side, if desired.
noteCook: When shopping for corned beef (or brisket, from which corned beef is made), you'll commonly see two cuts—flat (sometimes called thin) and point. Flat-cut is more uniformly shaped and thus will cook more evenly.

recipe.name: Courtesans
ingredients: Freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a medium bowl, place the goat cheese and set it aside to bring it up to room temperature, about 1 hour.

Meanwhile, trim the stems from the figs and slice an "X" into the top of each, going about three-quarters of the way through the fig so that the bottom remains intact. Use your index finger to make an indentation in the center of the cut side of the fig to keep the interior of the fruit exposed.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or foil. Arrange the cut figs on the prepared baking sheet and sprinkle each with a pinch of salt.

Once the cheese has softened, add 1 teaspoon of honey and the pistachios to the cheese and stir well with a fork. Add salt and pepper. Stuff each fig with about 1 teaspoon of the goat cheese mixture. Drizzle with olive oil and bake for 5 to 7 minutes, until the cheese looks soft and the figs begin to release their juices. Drizzle with the remaining tablespoon of honey and sprinkle with some more black pepper. Serve either warm or cold.
noteCook: If you're not a fan of the grassy pungency of goat cheese, swap it out with a milder ricotta.

recipe.name: Crakaneg

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg, plus extra for garnish

instructions: In a large bowl, beat the egg yolks with a whisk or an electric mixer until they begin to lighten in color and get a little fluffy, 1 to 2 minutes. Slowly add the sugar and continue to beat until fluffy and pale yellow. Set aside.

In a medium saucepan, combine the milk, cloves, cinnamon, and vanilla. Set the saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the milk mixture is steaming but not yet simmering or reads 155°F on an instant read thermometer. Remove from heat.

Slowly pour the milk into the egg mixture, whisking constantly to avoid curdling. Transfer the mixture back into the saucepan, set over medium heat, and cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture reaches 160°F, thickens slightly, and coats the back of the spoon, about 5 minutes.

Remove from the heat and stir in the cream. Pour the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer set over a pitcher to remove the cloves and cinnamon stick. Stir in the brandy and nutmeg. Let cool at room temperature for 1 hour. Then cover, transfer to the refrigerator, and chill for at least 1 hour, though the texture and flavor will improve the longer it rests. Serve in old-fashioned glasses garnished with grated nutmeg. Store any remaining mixture in an airtight jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

recipe.name: Craknoeg

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg, plus extra for garnish

instructions: In a blender, combine the cashew milk, coconut cream, dates, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, and salt. Blend on high for 1 to 2 minutes until smooth and creamy. Add the brandy and stir to combine. Transfer the mixture to the refrigerator and chill for at least 1 hour, though flavor will improve the longer it rests. Serve garnished with grated nutmeg. Store any remaining mixture in an airtight jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

recipe.name: Create Food and Water

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/c} medium garlic cloves, pressed or grated (about {=amount2/v} teaspoon)
{=amount1/v} medium scallions (white and green parts), trimmed and thinly sliced

instructions: Line a small rimmed baking sheet or cutting board with a clean dish towel or triple thickness of paper towels. Halve the tofu block lengthwise, cut each half into ½-inch-thick slices, and arrange on the lined baking sheet. Top the tofu with another clean dish towel or triple thickness of paper towels and a second baking sheet or small cutting board. Weigh it down with a large skillet or pot (or something of like weight) and set aside to drain, at least 20 minutes. In a wide, shallow dish, arrange the pressed tofu slices in a single layer.

Meanwhile, in a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, sesame oil, maple syrup, rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon of water, the gochujang, ginger, and garlic. Adjust the seasoning to taste with more of any of the ingredients. Pour the marinade over the tofu, turn the slices to coat (take care not to break them), cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 8 hours, turning over the slices about halfway through.
Arrange the marinated tofu on a serving dish if desired, sprinkle with the sesame seeds and scallions, and serve.
noteCook: Gochujang is a Korean spicy pepper paste with some umami and sweet flavor notes, but you can substitute any hot pepper sauce you'd like for it here.

recipe.name: Cremfels

ingredients.name: CREPES
entries: Kosher salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} cup milk, preferably whole (not skim), plus more, if necessary
{=amount1/v} tablespoons amber or dark rum (see Cook's Note)
{=amount1/v} tablespoons unsalted butter, cold and in a single chunk, plus extra for the pan, if necessary

instructions.name: Make the crepe batter:
entries: In a small bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, and ½ teaspoon of salt.

In a blender or food processor, process the eggs, ½ cup of the milk, and the rum until uniform, about 5 seconds. Stop the machine, add the flour mixture, and process to form a smooth batter, about 10 seconds. Stop and scrape down the sides of the blender jar or food processor work bowl. Add the remaining ½ cup of milk and continue to process until the mixture is very smooth and the consistency is a little thinner than that of heavy cream, about 10 seconds longer. Leave the batter in the blender jar or work bowl with the cover in place and rest for 15 minutes.

instructions.name: Make the creme:
entries: Meanwhile, with a handheld or standing mixer fitted with the whisk at medium speed, beat the cream until it begins to thicken, about 1 minute. Add the honey, crème fraîche, and vanilla. Adjust the speed to high and continue beating until the cream holds firm peaks, 1½ to 2 minutes longer in a standing mixer (you should have about 2⅔ cups). Cover and refrigerate until serving.

instructions.name: Cook and serve the crepes:
entries: Have on hand a large wire rack. Set a medium (10-inch) nonstick skillet over medium-low heat, and heat for 3 minutes. Melt the 3 tablespoons of butter in the skillet for 3 minutes. Swirl the skillet to coat the cooking surface with butter, pour the melted butter into the batter, and process to incorporate it. If the batter is thicker than heavy cream, add more milk, about 2 tablespoons at a time, and process briefly to adjust the consistency.

Return the skillet to the burner, adjust the heat to medium, and allow to heat for 1 minute longer. With a heat-safe silicone brush, brush the residual butter in the skillet to create a bare film of it on the cooking surface. Test the heat of the skillet—place 2 teaspoons of batter in the center and cook for about 20 seconds. Turn over the mini crepe with a heatproof nonstick-safe spatula. If it's spotty brown on the bottom, the skillet is properly heated; if it is too light or too dark, adjust the heat accordingly and retest.

When the skillet is properly heated, pour about 3 tablespoons of batter across the half of the skillet opposite the handle and, working very quickly, tilt and gently shake the skillet until the batter spreads across the cooking surface in a very thin, even, roughly 7-inch circle. Cook the crepe, undisturbed, until the top surface appears drier, the edges start to brown slightly, and the bottom is spotty brown, about 1 minute (or less, depending on your burner and skillet). With a spatula, loosen the crepe, carefully and gently grab the edge with your fingertips, flip it over, and cook until the second side is light golden brown, about 45 seconds to 1 minute longer. Transfer the cooked crepe to the wire rack with the more attractive, spotty brown side facing down, and cover loosely with foil.

Return the skillet to the heat. Repeat the process with the remaining crepe batter, adding another ½ teaspoon of butter, allowing it to melt, and brushing the cooking surface with it after every few crepes and adjusting the heat, if necessary. As each crepe finishes cooking, add it to the wire rack, with the more attractive sides facing down (you should have 12 to 14 crepes).

Working quickly, arrange 3 crepes on the work surface with the more attractive sides still facing down, dollop about 1 tablespoon of the creme in the center of each, fold each into quarters so the more attractive side is now visible, and arrange the 3 crepes on a serving plate. Continuing to work quickly, repeat with the remaining crepes and creme. Once all the crepes are filled, folded, and plated, dollop one-quarter of the remaining creme over each serving, top with about one-quarter of the raspberries, and serve immediately.

noteCook: You can use milk in place of the rum.

recipe.name: Curtie's Special

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons gochugaru (Korean red chili powder), or to taste
{=amount1/v} tablespoons gochujang (Korean chili paste), or to taste
{=amount1/c} garlic cloves, pressed or grated (about {=amount2/v} tablespoon)

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} hot dogs, bias-cut into roughly ¾-inch slices
{=amount1/xt} 14- to 20-ounce block firm tofu, drained and cut into 1-inch pieces
{=amount1/v} cup napa cabbage kimchi (about {=amount2/v} ounces), coarsely chopped
{=amount1/xt} 3- to 4-ounce package instant ramyun or ramen (noodles only; seasoning mix excluded)
{=amount1/v} medium scallions, whites thinly sliced and greens cut into roughly 2-inch lengths
{=amount1/v} or {=amount2/v} slices American cheese, preferably orange

ingredients: Fresh, hot white rice, for serving
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk the gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, garlic, ½ teaspoon of salt, pepper to taste, and ¼ cup of the broth until uniform. Set aside.

In a large, wide, medium-deep pot such as a braiser or saucier, scatter the onion. Arrange the SPAM, hot dogs, tofu, mushrooms, and kimchi in individual piles around the pot. Spoon the reserved gochugaru mixture over the piles and add the remaining 3¾ cups of broth and 1 cup of water (do not stir). Turn the burner to high, cover the pot, and bring the mixture to a rolling boil, about 8 minutes. Adjust the heat to medium-low, stir gently (trying to keep the separate piles intact as much as possible), partially cover, and simmer until all the ingredients are hot and the flavors have melded, about 10 minutes. Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper, if necessary.

Adjust the heat to low, nestle the noodles in the center of the pot, pushing them down just enough to almost but not entirely cover them. Spoon some broth over them, cover the pot, and cook, undisturbed, until the noodles are barely softened and starting to loosen, about 1½ minutes. Spoon some more broth over them and scatter the scallion greens around the noodles. Top the noodles with the cheese slices, cover, and allow the noodles to finish cooking (they should be chewy and loose, not soggy and distended) and the cheese to begin melting, about 2 minutes. Give the noodles and cheese a gentle stir, scatter the scallion whites over the stew, and serve immediately with a ladle and tongs, family-style, with rice.

recipe.name: Dark Molasses Nutbread

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup fine or medium-ground yellow cornmeal
{=amount1/v} cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle of the oven. Butter and flour an 8½ by 4½-inch loaf pan and tap out the excess (or coat with nonstick baking spray).
In a bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rye flour, cornmeal, baking soda, baking powder, and salt. Add the walnuts and stir to distribute.
In another bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, molasses, and melted butter (the butter will clump, which is fine).

Make a well in the center of the dry mixture, add the wet mixture, and, using a flexible spatula, fold and stir until the wet and dry ingredients are just incorporated (do not overmix). Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until the loaf is firm to the touch, the edges pull away from the pan slightly, and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool the bread in the pan on a wire rack for 20 minutes. Turn out the loaf, place it right-side up on the rack, and cool to room temperature. To serve, slice with a serrated knife.
noteCook: Rye flour is available from Bob's Red Mill and is sometimes found in the bulk department of a supermarket or natural foods store.

recipe.name: Deadwinter Fire
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ounces fresh ruby red grapefruit juice, plus 2 slices for garnish

instructions.name: To make the habanero-lime syrup:
entries: In a small saucepan, combine the water and sugar. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Add the habanero and lime zest, turn down the heat to low, and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and cool for 10 minutes. Strain the mixture into a fine-mesh strainer over a cup with a spout to remove the solids and set aside. Store any remaining habanero syrup in an airtight jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

instructions: Fill two highball glasses three-quarters full with ice. Divide the lime juice, 1 ounce of the habanero lime syrup, grapefruit juice, and tequila evenly between the two glasses. Top each with soda water and stir gently to combine. Make a 2-inch slit toward the center point of the grapefruit wheel and slide it onto the rim of each glass. Serve at once.
noteCook: Use disposable gloves when seeding the habanero to ensure that none of its fiery potency lingers on your fingers!

recipe.name: Deep Gnome Trillimac Pods

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup dry sherry, such as Amontillado
{=amount1/v} cup small pieces dried mushrooms, such as porcini or shiitake (optional)
{=amount1/v} ounces Italian Fontina cheese, shredded (about {=amount2/v} cup)

instructions: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, warm 1 tablespoon of the olive oil until shimmering. Add the cremini mushrooms and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushroom liquid evaporates and they just start to sizzle and brown, about 12 minutes. Adjust the heat to medium, clear the center of the pan, add another 1 tablespoon olive oil, and allow it to heat for a moment. Add half of the onion and ¼ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until the onion softens, about 4 minutes more; stir the onion into the mushrooms. Add half of the garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute more. Add the sherry and cook, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan to release and dissolve any browned bits, about 1 minute more. Scrape the ragout mixture into a bowl, add the parsley, and stir to incorporate. Set aside to cool to room temperature.

Wipe out the skillet, add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, return the pan to medium heat, and warm until shimmering. Add the remaining onion and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute more. Scrape the mixture into a medium bowl. Add the ricotta, egg, ½ cup of the Parmesan, ¼ teaspoon salt, and a few grinds of black pepper to the bowl. Stir until uniform, then set aside to cool to room temperature.

If you are using the dried mushrooms, in an electric spice grinder or mini food processor, pulverize the mushroom pieces until very, very fine and powdery. Add the powder to the ricotta mixture and stir until well blended.
In a small bowl, mix together the Fontina and remaining ½ cup Parmesan cheese.
Preheat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the middle of the oven. Coat a 12-cup muffin tin (preferably nonstick) with nonstick cooking spray.

To assemble, press one wonton wrapper into each cup, followed by about 1 tablespoon each of the ricotta mixture and mushroom ragout mixture, spreading each into an even layer. Add another wonton wrapper, rotating it slightly so the corners do not line up with the wrapper on the bottom. Repeat the layering with the remaining wonton wrappers and ricotta and mushroom ragout mixtures, always rotating the wonton wrappers, so the corners do not line up. Sprinkle about 1 tablespoon of the shredded cheese mixture evenly all the way to the edge of each cup; try to keep the cheese layer as thin as possible.

Bake until the cheese is melted, the edges of the wonton wrappers are browned, and the mini pies are hot all the way through, about 20 minutes, rotating the muffin tin 180 degrees halfway through the baking time.
Rest the mini pies for about 5 minutes. Use a dinner knife or small heatproof spatula to help remove them from the muffin cups (work carefully so they stay intact) and serve.

recipe.name: Delayed Blast Fireball

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, or more to taste

instructions: In a clean glass jar with a lid, combine the bourbon, red pepper flakes, and cinnamon sticks. Screw on the lid, shake, and store in a cool, dark place to infuse for 5 days, shaking the jar at least once a day.

In a bowl, whisk the brown sugar and hot water to dissolve the sugar fully and set aside to cool to room temperature, about 10 minutes. Line a fine-mesh strainer with cheesecloth, set it over the bowl with the brown sugar mixture, and strain the bourbon into it.
Wash and dry the jar and return the firestar wine to it. Serve or store in a cool, dark place for up to 3 months.
noteCook: The ½ teaspoon of crushed red pepper will provide a noticeable, moderate heat. If you prefer a more intense heat, use up to 1 teaspoon. You can give the drink more flavor nuance by replacing the crushed red pepper flakes with toasted chile. Toast half of a small dried California, pasilla, or guajillo chile in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, 4 to 5 minutes. Cool the chile and tear into very small (½-inch) pieces. For extra heat, use some of the chile seeds as well.
This drink can be enjoyed neat, over ice, mixed with cola, or as the foundation of an excellent hot toddy with spiced chai.

recipe.name: Delzoun "Tide-Me-Overs"

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} slices dark bread (such as rye), crusts discarded, remainder torn into pieces
{=amount1/v} tablespoons finely chopped fresh dill or parsley

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the cream and egg. Add the bread, mix well, and set aside, stirring occasionally, until the bread is softened, about 20 minutes. Using a fork or a sturdy spoon, mash the bread to a paste and set aside.

Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium heat, melt 1 tablespoon of the butter. Add the onion and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add the allspice and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Remove from the heat and let cool to room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 475°F with a rack in the middle of the oven. Coat a large wire rack with nonstick cooking spray and set it in a large rimmed baking sheet.
Add the cooled onion mixture, pork, ground beef, baking powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and ½ teaspoon pepper to the bread paste and, using a large spoon or your hands, mix until well combined and uniform.

With moistened hands, form the mixture into generous 1-tablespoon-size balls. Arrange the meatballs on the rack in the baking sheet and bake until lightly browned, about 20 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through.

Wipe out the skillet used for the onions to remove any stray onion bits, set it over medium heat, and melt the remaining 2 tablespoons butter. Stirring constantly, cook until fragrant and a shade darker, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the flour and cook, stirring constantly, until golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Switch to a whisk and, whisking constantly, gradually add the broth. Continuing to whisk often, cook for about 2 minutes. Add the brown sugar, soy sauce, lemon juice, and ¼ teaspoon pepper and continue to whisk and cook until thickened, about 2 minutes more.

Add the meatballs to the sauce and simmer, stirring occasionally, until heated through, about 4 minutes. Stir in most of the dill and taste and adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary. Transfer to a serving dish, sprinkle with the remaining dill, and serve hot.
noteCook: The sauce will thicken quickly as it cools. You can loosen the consistency by whisking in extra chicken broth or water, about 1 tablespoon at a time, until you have achieved the desired texture.

recipe.name: Double-High Halfling Pie

ingredients.name: CRUST

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoon unsalted butter, at room temperature, plus {=amount2/v} tablespoons, melted and still warm
{=amount1/v} whole graham crackers, broken into rough pieces
{=amount1/v} cup lightly packed light brown sugar

entries: Kosher salt

ingredients.name: RASPBERRY FILLING

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} cups (about {=amount2/v} ounces) fresh or frozen raspberries, thawed if frozen

entries: Kosher salt

ingredients.name: MANGO FILLING

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoons finely grated orange zest and {=amount2/v} cup fresh orange juice
{=amount1/v} cups peeled fresh or frozen mango chunks (about {=amount2/v} ounces frozen), thawed if frozen

entries: Kosher salt

instructions.name: Make the crust:
entries: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate with the room-temperature butter and set aside.

In a food processor, process the graham crackers to fine crumbs, about 25 seconds (you should have about a scant 3 cups crumbs). Add the brown sugar and ¼ teaspoon of salt and pulse to combine. With the motor running, slowly add the melted butter through the feed tube and process until the mixture resembles wet sand, about 30 seconds. Pour the mixture into the pie plate and press into an even, compact layer across the bottom and up the sides.

Bake the crust until lightly browned and fragrant, 12 to 15 minutes, rotating the pie plate about halfway through. Transfer to a wire rack and cool to room temperature (the crust will firm up as it cools).

instructions.name: Make the raspberry filling:
entries: Meanwhile, in a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and 3½ tablespoons of water until smooth and set aside. In a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, bring 1¼ cups of the raspberries, the sugar, and 1⁄8 teaspoon of salt to a bare simmer, stirring to dissolve the sugar, about 2 minutes. Whisk the cornstarch mixture again and add it to the pan, adjust the heat to medium, and cook, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan constantly, until the mixture thickens and reaches a gentle boil (you should see bubbles breaking the surface if you stop stirring for a moment), about 1 minute. Continue cooking at a gentle boil, stirring and scraping constantly and reaching into the corners of the pan, for 1 minute longer. Off heat, add the butter and vanilla, stir to melt and incorporate the butter, and set aside to cool for 15 minutes.

Add the remaining raspberries and fold to combine (you should have about 2 cups of filling). Scrape the filling into the pie shell, spread it evenly (all the way to the edges), smooth the top, and set aside to cool until barely warm, at least 20 minutes. Cover loosely with plastic wrap (take care not to crush the exposed edges of the crust) and refrigerate until well chilled and the filling is firm, at least 4 hours (or up to overnight).

instructions.name: Make the mango filling:
entries: After the raspberry filling has chilled and set firm, in a medium saucepan, stir the sugar and orange zest together until the sugar is moist and fragrant and set aside. In a food processor, puree the mango chunks until very smooth, about 40 seconds (you should have about 3¾ cups of puree), and scrape it into the pan with the sugar. In a small bowl, whisk the orange juice and cornstarch until smooth. Add it and ¼ teaspoon of salt to the mango-sugar mixture and whisk to combine. Set the pan over medium heat and, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan constantly, heat the mixture until it begins to thicken and reaches a gentle boil (you should see bubbles breaking the surface if you stop stirring for a moment), about 4½ minutes. Continue cooking at a gentle boil, stirring and scraping constantly and reaching into the corners of the pan, until the mixture reaches the consistency of thick pudding, about 5 minutes. Off heat, add the vanilla, stir to incorporate, and set aside to cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes (you should have about 3¾ cups of filling).

Scrape the filling into the pie plate over the chilled and set raspberry filling, spread it evenly all the way to the edges, and smooth the top. Cover with plastic wrap, pressing it loosely onto the surface (take care not to crush the exposed edges of the crust), and refrigerate until well chilled and the filling is firm, at least 4 hours (or up to overnight).

instructions.name: Make the whipped cream topping:
entries: Near serving time, remove the pie from the refrigerator to rest at room temperature to lose its chill. With a handheld or standing mixer fitted with the whisk at medium speed, beat the cream until it begins to thicken, about 1 minute. Add the sugar and vanilla, adjust the speed to high, and continue beating until the cream holds stiff peaks, about 2½ minutes longer in a standing mixer. Dollop the whipped cream over the mango filling, spreading it all the way to the edges into a thick, even layer, and smooth the top. Serve.

noteCook: Both fillings need a few hours to chill and set, so start making the pie early if you want to serve it that day or, better yet, the day before.

recipe.name: Dour Bread

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature, cut into 4 pieces

ingredients: Neutral oil, to grease a bowl and a work surface
instructions: In a small saucepan over medium heat, bring the milk to a bare simmer. Add the butter and swirl the pan to melt and incorporate it. Off the heat, set the pan aside and cool the mixture until lukewarm (about 105° to 110°F).

To a stand mixer fitted with the paddle, add the flour, sugar, yeast, and salt and mix on low speed to combine. Add the lukewarm milk mixture, the eggs, and vanilla and mix at low speed until well combined. Switch to the dough hook and mix on low speed until the dough is smooth, soft, and slightly sticky, 8 to 10 minutes.

Put the dough in a lightly greased large bowl, flipping the dough once to grease the top and bottom. Cover with a clean kitchen towel and set aside in a warm place to rise until doubled in size, 60 to 90 minutes.

Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside. Have a second sheet of parchment paper and a second baking sheet on hand. Lightly oil a work surface, turn out the dough onto it, and pat out the dough gently. With a bench knife, divide the dough into ten equal pieces. With a loosely cupped hand, roll each piece into a tight ball. Arrange them on the work surface with about 1 inch between them, cover them with the kitchen towel or plastic wrap, and rest for 30 minutes.

Gently press the dough balls into circles about 4 to 5 inches in diameter and ½ inch thick. Arrange them on the prepared baking sheet with at least 1½ inches between them. Position the second piece of parchment paper followed by the second baking sheet over the dough. Set the assembly aside in a warm place for the dough to rise to about ¾ inch thick, about 45 minutes.

Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F. Bake, keeping the top parchment paper and baking sheet in place, for 9 minutes. Remove the top baking sheet and parchment paper, flip over the buns, reassemble the top parchment and baking sheet, and continue baking until the buns are deep golden brown on the top and bottom, 6 to 9 minutes longer. Transfer the buns to a wire rack to cool and then serve. They're best eaten day of, but if well wrapped, they'll keep at room temperature for up to 3 days.

recipe.name: Dragon Salmon

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds skin-on salmon fillet, pinbones removed if necessary, cut crosswise into {=amount2/v} equal pieces, and blotted dry

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons neutral-tasting oil, such as vegetable, canola, safflower, or grapeseed
{=amount1/v} cup fruity, medium-bodied red wine, such as Pinot Noir, Côtes du Rhône, or Zinfandel
{=amount1/v} tablespoons minced fresh chives for garnish

instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°F with a rack in the middle of the oven.
Sprinkle the salmon lightly with salt and pepper.

In a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, warm the oil until shimmering. Add the salmon flesh-side down, leaving at least ¼ inch of space around the pieces, and cook, undisturbed, until the bottoms of the fillets start to turn opaque, 3 to 4 minutes. Gently flip the fillets skin-side down, and cook, again undisturbed, until they are no longer translucent on the exterior and are firm when gently pressed, about 3 minutes for rare or 4 minutes for medium. Transfer the salmon to a heatproof plate, tent loosely with foil, and place it in the oven to keep warm.

Wipe out the skillet, add 1 tablespoon of the butter, and melt it over medium-low heat. Add the shallot, thyme, and ¼ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring constantly, until the shallot softens, about 1 minute. Add the wine and broth, adjust the heat to medium-high, and bring the mixture to a simmer, occasionally stirring and scraping the bottom of the skillet to loosen and dissolve any browned bits. Continue simmering until reduced by about two-thirds, 6 to 8 minutes longer, adding any accumulated salmon juices midway through. Adjust the heat to low, add the remaining 1 tablespoon butter, ¼ teaspoon salt, and pepper to taste. And stir constantly while the butter melts and incorporates into the sauce. Taste and adjust the seasoning with additional salt, if necessary. Pour or spoon the sauce over or around the salmon, sprinkle with the chives, and serve hot.

recipe.name: Dragonberries

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cans of chickpeas, drained and rinsed
{=amount1/v} teaspoon garlic powder or granulated garlic

instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.

Spread the drained chickpeas over a layer of paper towels or a dish towel. Layer another towel on top of the chickpeas and pat them dry. Transfer them into a medium bowl and add the cumin, paprika, chili powder, coriander, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne pepper, salt, and olive oil. Toss to coat.
Spread the chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until crispy. Remove from the oven and let fully cool before serving.

recipe.name: Dragonfire Mead

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} thin slices (about ⅜-inch-thick) Fresno or serrano chile, with seeds

ingredients: Ice, preferably cracked or small cubes
instructions: Cut 2 thin slices from the center of the lime, make a small cut in each (so they can be placed on the rim of a glass), and set aside. Spread the Tajín on a small plate.

Run one of the lime halves along the rims of two tumblers or rocks glasses and dip the rims into the Tajín, turning the glasses to coat the rims lightly and evenly (you'll have some Tajín left over). Set the glasses aside.
In a small bowl, squeeze the lime halves and the second lime, if necessary, to yield 2 ounces of juice.

Add the chile slices and sugar to a medium (about 24 ounces) cocktail shaker. With a muddler, muddle until the chile is broken down and the sugar is dissolved. Fill the shaker about halfway with ice and add the lime juice, honey syrup, mezcal, and mead. Cover and shake to blend and chill, at least 15 seconds.
Fill the two prepared glasses about halfway with ice and divide the mixture between them. Place one of the lime slices on the rim of each glass to garnish and serve immediately.

recipe.name: Drow Mushroom Steaks

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} large portobello mushrooms caps (stems removed and discarded)

instructions: In a shallow dish wide enough to hold the mushrooms in a single layer, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, balsamic vinegar, thyme, salt, and several grinds of pepper. Put the mushrooms in the dish. Set aside to marinate at room temperature for 15 minutes, turning the mushrooms over and spooning the marinade on them halfway through.
Heat an outdoor grill or indoor grill pan over medium-high heat. Grill the mushrooms, flipping to cook both sides, until tender and browned, 10 to 12 minutes. Serve hot or at room temperature.

recipe.name: Druid Winter Cocktail

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} sprigs fresh rosemary, about 2 inches longer than the height of the serving glasses
{=amount1/v} teaspoons liquid edible glitter, or {=amount2/v} teaspoon dry edible glitter

instructions: Cut 2 thin slices from the center of the lime, make a small cut in each (so they can be placed on the rim of a glass), and set aside.

Stab 1 rosemary sprig into the cut side of each lime half so that it stands upright. Press 1 of the rosemary-lime halves firmly into the bottom of each of two narrow Collins or highball glasses (or other type of glass the bottom circumference of which matches the circumference of the lime halves) so the rosemary sprigs stand upright in the center of the glasses.

Carefully fill each glass about halfway with ice cubes, dropping them slowly all around the rosemary sprigs. Pour 2 ounces of gin into each glass. Add the tonic and glitter to a third glass, stir to distribute the glitter, and immediately pour half into each glass with the gin. Place 1 of the lime slices on the rim of each glass to garnish, add a swizzle stick to each, and serve immediately, instructing recipients to stir their drinks to combine the components and agitate the glitter for a shimmery visual effect.
noteCook: Your chosen glass should be clear, without a tint or pattern, and the circumference of the base must match the circumference of the lime, so that the cut lime will sit very snug in the bottom of the glass, even when the liquids are added.
Glitter comes liquid, dry, and as a spray and in many colors; for this drink, either silver or white is a good choice.

recipe.name: Duergar Smoked Herring

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons neutral oil or extra-virgin olive oil
{=amount1/v} red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped
{=amount1/v} Cubanelle pepper or a small green bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped
{=amount1/v} Scotch bonnet or habanero chile, pricked all over with a fork
{=amount1/v} scallions (white and green parts), thinly sliced
{=amount1/v} tablespoon fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving

instructions: In a large skillet over medium heat, warm the neutral oil until shimmering. Add the onion, red bell pepper, Cubanelle pepper, Scotch bonnet, and 1 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring, until fragrant and a shade darker, about 1½ minutes. Add the thyme and garlic and cook, stirring until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften, about 3 minutes. Add the kippers and cook, stirring occasionally and taking care not to completely shred the fish (though it will break down some as you stir, which is fine), until heated through, about 3 minutes longer. Add most of the scallions and the lime juice and season with black pepper, stirring to incorporate.

Remove the skillet from the heat and discard the whole chile. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary. Serve immediately, sprinkling each portion with some of the remaining scallions and a lime wedge on the side.
noteCook: Sliced avocado and sliced hard-boiled egg are nice accompaniments. This easily becomes a full meal when served with rice and a salad.

recipe.name: Duskmallow Pie

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoons unsalted butter, softened, plus {=amount2/v} tablespoons, melted and warm
{=amount1/v} cups/{=amount2/v} ounces gingersnaps, divided broken into rough pieces
{=amount1/v} ounces cream cheese, at room temperature and cut into small pieces

instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-inch pie plate with 2 teaspoons of the softened butter and set aside.

Reserve ¼ cup of the gingersnaps and set aside until serving time. In a food processor, process the remaining 3¾ cups of gingersnaps to fine crumbs, about 20 seconds. Add the brown sugar and a pinch of salt and pulse to combine. With the motor running, slowly add the melted butter and process until the mixture resembles wet sand, about 20 seconds. Pour the mixture into the pie plate and press into an even, compact layer across the bottom and up the sides. Bake until fragrant and slightly darker, about 12 minutes, rotating the pie plate about halfway through baking. Transfer to a wire rack and cool to room temperature.

Meanwhile, in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat, warm the milk, marshmallows, and a tiny pinch of salt, constantly stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan with a heatproof, flexible spoonula to prevent sticking, until the marshmallows are fully melted and the mixture is uniform, 4 to 6 minutes. Off the heat, add the cream cheese and vanilla and stir to melt and incorporate the cream cheese until smooth, about 2 minutes. Cool the mixture to room temperature, about 25 minutes, stirring and scraping occasionally during that time.

When the marshmallow mixture is nearly cooled, with a standing mixer fitted with the whisk at medium speed, beat the cream until it begins to thicken. Adjust the speed to high and continue beating until the cream holds stiff peaks, about 1 minute longer. Scrape the whipped cream into the cooled marshmallow mixture and use the spoonula to fold them together until uniform. Scrape the filling into the pie shell, spread it evenly, smooth the top, cover loosely with plastic wrap, and refrigerate until the filling is firm, at least 4 hours (or up to overnight).
Near serving time, remove the pie from the refrigerator to lose its chill. Chop the reserved gingersnaps into pea-size pieces, sprinkle them on the pie to garnish, and serve.

recipe.name: Dwarven Flatbread

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
{=amount1/v} teaspoons dried herb blend (such as Italian seasoning, herbes de Provence, or za'atar), crushed
{=amount1/v} cup plain low-fat Greek yogurt or whole milk
{=amount1/v} cup neutral-tasting oil, such as vegetable, canola, safflower, or grapeseed

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and herb blend to combine. Make a well in the center, add the olive oil and yogurt. With a wooden spoon or your hands, stir around the perimeter of the well to incorporate the wet and dry ingredients; the mixture will look a little rough and shaggy.

Lightly flour a work surface, scoop the dough onto it, and knead until the dough is smooth and uniform, adding a tiny amount of flour as you go if the dough becomes too sticky. Divide the dough into eight equal portions, gently roll each portion into a ball, cover with a clean kitchen towel, and let rest for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200°F (or the lowest temperature possible) with a rack in the middle of the oven.

With a rolling pin, roll one of the dough balls into a circle about 7 inches in diameter and ¼ inch thick. In a 10-inch heavy skillet (preferably cast iron) over medium heat, warm 1½ teaspoons of the vegetable oil until shimmering. Tilt the skillet to coat the entire cooking surface with oil, carefully place the dough circle in the skillet, and cook, undisturbed, until spotty brown on the bottom and slightly puffed, 3 to 4 minutes. Turn the bread over and continue to cook, undisturbed, until the second side is spotty brown as well, 3 to 4 minutes more. Transfer the bread to a baking sheet or ovenproof plate and place it in the oven to stay warm. Working with one dough ball and 1½ teaspoons oil at a time, repeat to roll, cook, and keep the remaining rounds warm. Note that as the pan accumulates and retains heat from previous batches, the cooking time may decrease by up to a minute. Serve warm and fresh
noteCook: Skillet breads are a great canvas for customizing with simple toppings, such as finely chopped roasted red pepper or caramelized onions, or a schmear of ricotta cheese, added just before serving.

recipe.name: Dwarven Mulled Wine

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup packed light brown sugar, or to taste
{=amount1/v} ({=amount2/v}-ml) bottle medium-bodied, fruity red wine, such as Merlot or Syrah

instructions: Using a vegetable peeler, remove the zest from the oranges in wide strips; reserve one strip for each drink and refrigerate, covered, until serving time. Stick the cloves into two or three of the remaining zest strips and set aside. Cut the zested oranges in half and juice them (which should yield about ¾ cup juice).

In a large saucepan over medium heat, bring the orange juice and brown sugar to a simmer, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Add the wine, cinnamon stick, and orange zest (including the clove-studded pieces) and bring to a simmer. Adjust the heat to medium-low and simmer, partially covered and stirring occasionally, until the wine is fragrant and infused, about 1 hour (do not allow it to boil). Add the vanilla and brandy and continue to simmer, stirring occasionally, to blend the flavors, about 2 minutes more. Taste and adjust the flavor with additional brown sugar and/or brandy, if necessary. With a slotted spoon, remove and discard the cinnamon stick, orange zest, and cloves.

Meanwhile, fill one small mug or heatproof glass for each drinker with hot water to preheat them, about 2 minutes. Empty the mugs or glasses, ladle some of the wine into each, garnish with one of the reserved orange zest strips, and serve at once.
noteCook: The flavor of mulled wine improves with rest, so consider starting it several hours ahead of time. Reheat it gently, careful to avoid boiling (which can cause an oxidized taste), then remove the aromatics and add the vanilla and brandy.

Mulled wine recipes vary widely. This one is heavy on the orange, light on the spice and sweetener, and includes brandy for a modest potency boost. However, it can be customized with different liqueurs such as Grand Marnier, Cointreau, or St-Germain, and spices such as cardamom pods, black peppercorns, or whole allspice.

recipe.name: Eel Rolls with Sticky Rice

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} at least 8-ounce package frozen precooked eel, semi-thawed
{=amount1/xt} 7½ by 8-inch sheets nori, each cut in half crosswise
{=amount1/v} tablespoons sesame seeds, lightly toasted and cooled
About {=amount1/v} English cucumber, peeled, seeded, and cut into very thin (about ⅜-inch-thick) strips
About {=amount1/v} cup prepared sushi ginger, blotted dry with paper towels

instructions.name: Make the eel sauce:
entries: In a medium skillet over medium heat, bring the mirin, sake, soy sauce, and agave to a steamy simmer, swirling the skillet, 2½ to 3 minutes. Continue simmering, swirling the pan occasionally, until it is fragrant. A tight, glossy, foamy layer of bubbles covers most of the surface, and running your finger across the back of a spoon coated with sauce leaves a clean trail, 5½ to 6½ minutes longer.
Off the heat, cool the mixture to room temperature (it will thicken; you should have about a scant ½ cup).

In a small saucepan over low heat, swirl the vinegar, sugar, and salt until the sugar and salt dissolve completely, about 1½ to 2 minutes (do not boil). Off the heat, allow the mixture to cool while washing and cooking the rice.

Wash and cook the rice. In a medium bowl, cover the rice with 1¼ cups of cold water by about 2 inches. Using your fingers, gently swirl and agitate the rice until the water becomes cloudy and white. Immediately strain the rice, return it to the bowl, and wash four or five more times, until the water appears much less cloudy and white after agitating the rice. After straining the rice for the last time, set the strainer over the bowl and rest the rice for 5 minutes (the small amount of water that collects in the bowl should be clear).

Add the drained, rested rice and the water to a medium saucepan (preferably nonstick) and soak the rice for 30 minutes. Set the pan over medium heat, cover, and bring to a strong simmer, about 6 minutes. Adjust the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Off the heat, rest the rice, leaving the cover in place (to keep accumulated steam in the pan) until the rice is tender and has absorbed all the water, about 12 minutes (you will have about 3½ cups cooked rice).

Meanwhile, while the rice rests, rinse a large bowl (preferably wooden) and a rice paddle or wooden spatula with cool water and lightly dry them with a clean kitchen towel, leaving a bare film of moisture (to help prevent the rice from sticking). Use the paddle to loosen the rice around the edges of the pot, then overturn the pot into the prepared bowl and sharply shake it to release the rice. Using the prepared rice paddle, lightly scrape any loose rice that remains in the pot into the bowl (but do not scrape off any rice that sticks hard to the bottom of the pan).

Season the rice. Holding the paddle roughly parallel to the rice in the bowl, pour the cooled sushi vinegar over the paddle so it drips slowly onto the rice, moving the paddle as you pour to distribute the vinegar evenly onto the rice. Continuing to hold the paddle parallel to the rice, slice into the rice and fold it to incorporate the vinegar, cool the rice, and break down any small clumps, about 2 minutes (try to keep the rice as fluffy as possible; the rice will appear quite damp at first but look drier as you continue to work the vinegar into it). Gently scrape the rice to one side of the bowl, cover it with a clean, dampened kitchen towel pressed gently onto the rice to prevent it from drying out while you prepare the rolls, and rest for about 15 minutes.

Prepare the eel and chiles for the rolls. Line a baking sheet with foil, spray it with nonstick cooking spray, and set aside. With the rack about 6 inches below the heating element, preheat the broiler. Hold the semi-frozen eel under a gentle stream of cool running water to wash away the sauce (take care not to break the delicate fillet). Lay it skin-side down on a work surface and, with paper towels, wipe both sides of the eel dry. Cut the fillet in half lengthwise, then holding the knife at a 45-degree angle to the eel and on a gentle bias, cut each half into 1-inch slices. Place the slices skin-side up on the prepared baking sheet and broil until the eel sizzles gently and the skin becomes crisp, 9 to 10 minutes. Remove from the broiler, carefully remove the eel slices to a plate (they may stick to the foil a bit), and set aside.

Cut each chile in half crosswise. Remove the cores and seeds from the thicker ends of each chile, cut them into thin strips, and set aside. Cut the thinner ends into very thin slices (at least 32) and set aside separately.

instructions.name: Prepare the eel rolls:
entries: Have on hand a bamboo mat for rolling sushi (makisu), a cutting board, a bowl of cold water, a wet, clean kitchen towel, and plastic wrap. With the bamboo slats in the mat perpendicular to the box of plastic wrap, wrap the mat tightly in at least two layers of plastic. Lay the wrapped mat on a cutting board with the slats parallel to the bottom of your cutting board and smoother side facing up.

Lay a piece of nori on the wrapped mat with the rougher side facing up and the bottom edge at least 1½ inches from the bottom of the mat. Wet your hands (to prevent the sushi rice from sticking to them) and put about ⅔ cup of rice on the nori. Wet your fingers to prevent sticking, and using mostly your thumbs, gently push the rice into an even layer on the nori, all the way to the edges, rewetting your fingers as necessary. Sprinkle the rice evenly with 1½ teaspoons of the sesame seeds and turn over the nori so the rice is on the bottom against the mat.

Spread about 1 tablespoon of the eel sauce lengthwise down the center of the nori. Arrange 3 or 4 pieces of the eel lengthwise and skin-side up over the sauce, leaving about 1½ inches to the bottom edge of the nori. Tuck a few strips of cucumber along the bottom edge of the eel and a few strips of chile and slices of ginger along the top edge of the eel, all the way to the side edges of the nori.

Holding the ingredients in place with your fingertips, use your thumbs to roll the mat from the bottom edge up so the bottom edge of the nori just covers the ingredients (the edge of the mat will reach just beyond the top edge of the ingredients and the top edge of the nori will still be visible). Pull the top of the mat away from you as you continue rolling, applying even, moderate pressure with your fingers to create a tight roll with the nori sealed at the bottom. If necessary, use the mat to further smooth and refine the shape of the roll and to neaten the ends.

Dampen the blade of your knife to help prevent sticking and cut the roll in half. Wiping off and dampening the blade again between each cut, cut the halves in half to create 4 pieces, and cut each of those 4 pieces in half to create 8 pieces. Again, use the mat to further refine the shape of the roll and to neaten the ends. Arrange the pieces attractively on a serving plate.
Repeat with the remaining nori sheets, sushi rice, sesame seeds, eel, cucumber, and chopped ginger and chile to create and cut 3 more rolls, arranging the pieces on the serving platter as you go.
Dab the top of each piece of the roll very lightly with eel sauce, place a slice of chile over the dab to garnish, and serve immediately.

noteCook: If the eel sauce becomes too thick once it has cooled fully, set the pan over medium-low heat briefly, just until it's pourable again.
For cutting the sushi rolls, make sure your knife is super sharp and use long strokes to slice without too much pressure, which can push the rolls out of shape.

recipe.name: Eggplant Steaks with Harelveauplum Sauce

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds eggplant, peeled, stem ends trimmed, and cut lengthwise into ¾-inch-thick slices

ingredients.name: CHUNKY HARVELVEAUPLUM SAUCE

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} medium yellow onion, diced large (about ¾- to 1-inch pieces)
{=amount1/v} medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and diced large (about ¾- to 1-inch pieces)

entries: Kosher salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} medium dark plums (about {=amount2/v} inches; about {=amount3/v} ounces), pitted and diced large (about ½-inch pieces; about {=amount1/v} cups)
{=amount1/c} large garlic clove, pressed or grated (about {=amount1/v} teaspoon)
{=amount1/v} tablespoon finely chopped (seeded, if desired) Fresno chile
{=amount1/v} tablespoon sherry, cider, or red wine vinegar
{=amount1/v} tablespoons honey, or more, to taste (see Cook's Note)
{=amount1/v} tablespoons chopped mixed fresh herbs, such as parsley, basil, chives, mint, and scallion greens

entries: Freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Line two rimmed baking sheets with clean kitchen towels or a triple layer of paper towels. Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of salt evenly over both sides of the eggplant slices to draw out its water and arrange the eggplant in single layers on the lined baking sheets. Allow to drain for about 1 hour, flipping the slices halfway through. Blot the eggplant dry with another clean kitchen towel or triple layer of paper towels, pressing firmly but taking care not to crush the eggplant. Transfer the eggplant to a bowl or plate and set aside. Wash and dry the baking sheets.

With the racks in the upper- and lower-middle positions, place a baking sheet on each rack and preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a large platter or third baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.

In a wide, shallow dish such as a pie plate, whisk together the flour and 1 teaspoon of black pepper. In a second wide, shallow dish, beat the eggs until uniform. In the third wide, shallow dish, combine the breadcrumbs, paprika, garlic and onion powders, cayenne, ½ teaspoon of salt, and 1 teaspoon of black pepper, and stir to blend.

Working with 1 or 2 eggplant slices at a time, dredge them in the flour and tap off any excess. Dip the floured slices into the egg to coat thoroughly, allowing any excess to drip into the dish. Then dredge in the panko mixture to coat thoroughly, pressing the panko onto the eggplant to help it adhere. Place the slices on the prepared platter or baking sheet and repeat with the remaining eggplant slices, trying not to overlap them.

Carefully remove the preheated baking sheets from the oven. Add ¼ cup of the oil to each sheet and, using a heat-resistant silicone brush, carefully spread it out evenly. Place half the breaded eggplant slices on each sheet in a single layer. Bake for 20 minutes, then flip the slices, rotating the baking sheets and swapping between the racks. Continue baking until the eggplant is well browned and crisp, 20 to 25 minutes longer.

instructions.name: Make the Harvelveauplum sauce:
entries: Meanwhile, in a medium skillet over medium heat, warm the olive oil until shimmering. Add the onion, bell pepper, and ½ teaspoon of salt and cook, stirring, until the vegetables begin to soften, about 6 minutes. Add the plums and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables and plums are tender, about 7 minutes longer, adding ¼ cup of water about halfway through. Add the garlic and Fresno chile and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Add the vinegar and honey and cook, stirring, to melt and incorporate the honey, about 1 minute. Remove from the heat and set aside to cool briefly. Add the herbs and black pepper to taste and stir to incorporate. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and black pepper, if necessary.

instructions: Sprinkle the eggplant slices with black pepper and very lightly with salt, if desired. Transfer to a serving platter, spoon the Harvelveauplum sauce over or around the eggplant, and serve immediately.
noteCook: Depending on the sweetness of your plums, you may want to use more or less honey, so take a small nibble of your plums to help you decide.

recipe.name: Eldeen Banquet

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds eggplant, peeled, stem ends trimmed, and cut lengthwise into ¾-inch-thick slices

ingredients.name: Sautéed Tomatoes
entries: Kosher salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} cups cherry tomatoes or large grape tomatoes, halved

instructions: Line two baking sheets with clean kitchen towels or a triple layer of paper towels.

Sprinkle 1 tablespoon salt evenly over both sides of the eggplant slices to draw out its water and arrange the eggplant in a single layer on the prepared baking sheets. Allow to drain for about 1 hour, flipping the slices halfway through. Blot the eggplant dry with another clean kitchen towel or triple layer of paper towels, pressing firmly but taking care not to crush the eggplant. Transfer to a bowl or plate, and set aside. Wash and dry the baking sheets.
With racks in the upper- and lower-middle positions, place a baking sheet on each rack, and preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a large platter or third baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.

In a shallow dish, such as a pie plate, combine the flour and 1 teaspoon pepper and whisk to incorporate. In a second shallow dish, beat the eggs until uniform. In a third shallow dish, combine the panko, oregano, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, ½ teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper and stir to blend.

Working with one or two eggplant slices at a time, dredge them in the flour and tap off any excess. Dip the floured slices into the egg to coat thoroughly, allowing any excess to drip into the dish. Then dredge in the panko mixture to coat thoroughly, pressing the panko onto the eggplant to help adhere. Place the slices on the prepared platter, and repeat with the remaining eggplant slices, trying not to overlap them.

Carefully remove the preheated baking sheets from the oven. Add ¼ cup of the olive oil to each sheet and, using a heatproof silicone brush, spread it out evenly. Place half the breaded eggplant slices on each baking sheet in a single layer. Bake for 20 minutes and then flip the slices, rotating the baking sheets, and swap between the racks. Continue baking until the eggplant is well browned and crisp, 20 to 25 minutes longer.

instructions.name: To make the tomatoes:
entries: About 10 minutes after flipping the eggplant slices, in a medium skillet over medium heat, warm the olive oil. Add the shallot and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring constantly, until the shallot starts to soften, about 2 minutes. Add the garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Add the tomatoes, shake the pan to coat them with oil, and cook, shaking the skillet occasionally, until they soften but do not collapse completely, about 4 minutes, adding the sugar halfway through cooking. Add the vinegar and parsley and toss to distribute. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt if necessary.

instructions: Sprinkle the baked eggplant very lightly with salt. Transfer to a serving platter, spoon the tomatoes over or around the eggplant, and sprinkle with parsley. Serve immediately.
noteCook: You'll need at least two, and preferably three, baking sheets. If you don't have a third, you can use a large cutting board for the dredged eggplant slices.
