Transfer the mushrooms to a serving plate and spoon some of the butter from the pan over them. Sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper to taste and the parsley and serve immediately.

recipe.name: Oysters and Wild Rice in Mushroom Soup

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup wild rice, rinsed well in a strainer
{=amount1/v} pound cremini mushrooms, cleaned, trimmed, and thinly sliced
{=amount1/v} medium leek (about {=amount2/v} ounces) (white and light green parts), quartered lengthwise and sliced crosswise into ¼-inch pieces (about {=amount3/v} cups)
{=amount1/v} medium rib celery, trimmed and finely chopped (about {=amount1/v} cup)
{=amount1/xt} 3.75-ounce cans smoked oysters, drained and blotted dry with paper towels
{=amount1/v} tablespoons finely chopped chives or celery leaves, for garnish

instructions: In a medium saucepan over high heat, bring 4 cups of water to a boil. Add the rice, bay leaf, and ½ teaspoon of salt and return to the boil. Adjust the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, 40 to 60 minutes. Set a fine-mesh strainer in a medium heatproof bowl or large measuring cup and strain the rice. Remove and reserve the bay leaf, and reserve both the rice and the cooking liquid.

In a large, heavy pot over medium-high heat, melt 1 tablespoon of the butter, swirling to coat the pan. Add the mushrooms and ½ teaspoon of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushroom liquid evaporates and the mushrooms start to sizzle and brown, about 12 minutes. Scrape the mushrooms into the strainer with the rice.

Return the pot to medium heat, add ½ cup of the reserved rice cooking liquid, and warm it, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan to loosen and dissolve any browned bits. Return the liquid to the rest.

Wipe out the pot, return it to medium heat, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and melt, swirling to coat the pan. Add the leek, celery, thyme, reserved bay leaf, and ½ teaspoon of salt and cook, stirring, until the vegetables are softened but not browned, about 6 minutes. Add the rice, mushrooms, half-and-half, and 1½ cups of rice cooking liquid. Adjust the heat to medium and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring, about 12 minutes. Off heat, cover and rest so the flavors can meld, about 15 minutes.

Add the smoked oysters and pepper to taste. Return the pot to medium heat and warm, stirring occasionally, until both the liquid and the oysters are warm, about 8 minutes. Remove and discard the bay leaf and adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper as necessary. Ladle into individual bowls, sprinkle each portion with some of the chives or celery leaves, and serve.
noteCook: If the mushrooms pile up in the pot, they may not brown properly, so consider cooking them in two batches, using ½ tablespoon of butter for each.

recipe.name: Pan-Fried Fungi with Garlic Butter

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds cremini mushrooms, cleaned and quartered (about {=amount2/v} cups)
{=amount1/v} garlic cloves, pressed or grated (about {=amount2/v} teaspoons)
{=amount1/v} cup brandy or cognac (see Cook's Note)

instructions: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, combine the mushrooms and 1 teaspoon of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushroom liquid evaporates and they begin to brown, about 14 minutes, adjusting the heat as necessary to avoid scorching. Using a wooden spoon, clear the center of the skillet. Melt the butter in the clearing, add the shallots, and cook, stirring, until they begin to soften, about 2 minutes. Stir the shallots into the mushrooms, add the garlic and thyme, and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Add the brandy and stir and scrape the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon to dissolve any browned bits. Add the pepper and parsley, stir to distribute it, and serve.
noteCook: You can use chicken or vegetable broth, or white wine or vermouth, in place of the brandy to deglaze the pan.

recipe.name: Pan-Fried Knucklehead Trout
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ({=amount2/v}-ounce) rainbow trout fillets, skin on, rinsed and dried well

instructions: Preheat the oven to 250°F with a rack in the middle of the oven.
In a wide, shallow dish such as a pie plate, whisk together the flour, paprika, ½ teaspoon salt, and ½ teaspoon pepper.
Sprinkle the trout fillets lightly with salt and pepper and let rest until they appear moist and glistening, about 5 minutes.

In a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, warm the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter, swirling to combine, until melted and hot. Dredge the fillets in the flour mixture, coat thoroughly, and tap off the excess. Carefully place each fillet, flesh-side down, in the skillet. Cook until the edges are opaque and bottoms are golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Carefully turn the fillets over with a spatula and continue to cook until the second side is golden brown and opaque, 2 to 3 minutes more (if the skillet begins to smoke, adjust the heat to medium). Carefully transfer the fillets to an ovenproof serving platter and keep warm in the oven.
Juice one of the lemon halves and cut the other half into four wedges.

Cut the remaining 4 tablespoons butter into four pieces and melt in a small skillet over medium-high heat. Add the shallot, stirring constantly until the butter is golden brown and fragrant with a nutty aroma, about 2 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the lemon juice, ½ teaspoon salt, and pepper to taste and swirl the pan to combine. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper, if necessary. Pour the browned butter over the fish, sprinkle with the parsley, and serve at once with the lemon wedges.

recipe.name: Par-Salian's Tea

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v}-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled if desired

instructions: Using a vegetable peeler and working vertically, remove the zest from the lemon in wide strips (it should produce eight strips). Slice the ginger into four pieces, each about ½ inch thick, and working with one slice at a time, use the bottom of a sturdy mug or the flat side of a chef's knife to smash them. Place two lemon zest strips and one piece of smashed ginger in each of four mugs. Add about 1¼ cups boiling water to each mug and steep until fragrant, about 4 minutes. Add honey to taste to each mug and stir to combine. Holding the mint sprigs by their stems, slap them against the back of your hand or forearm (to help release their fragrance). Add one sprig to each mug and serve.
noteCook: Peeling the ginger isn't strictly necessary.

The ginger and lemon zest will continue to infuse the liquid as you drink. For the strongest flavor, leave them in the mug until you finish; remove them at any point when you find the flavor sufficiently potent.

recipe.name: Pegasus

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} fresh mint leaves, plus {=amount2/v} sprigs for garnish

ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes

instructions.name: To make the ginger syrup:
entries: In a small saucepan, bring the ginger, sugar, and water to a boil over medium-high heat. Lower the heat and bring the mixture to a simmer. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes. Turn off the heat and steep for 30 minutes. Let the syrup fully cool before using. Store any remaining ginger syrup in an airtight jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

instructions: In a mixing glass, muddle the peaches, mint leaves, and lemon juice until the peaches are well broken down. Add 1 ounce of ginger syrup and the bourbon and fill halfway with ice. Using a long-handled spoon, stir until well chilled, about 30 seconds. Completely fill two highball glasses with crushed ice. Strain and divide the mixture evenly between the two glasses. Top with a dash of bitters and garnish with a mint sprig. Serve at once.
noteCook: If you want to make this cocktail outside of peach season, frozen peaches work just as well! Simply fully thaw before using to enjoy vibrant peach flavor all year long.

ingredients.name: PICKLED BEANS/VINE BLIGHT
entries: Kosher salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds green beans, washed and trimmed to fit into jars
{=amount1/v} cup distilled white or white wine vinegar
{=amount1/v} garlic cloves, peeled and crushed lightly

ingredients.name: SALAD
entries: Kosher salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoons white wine or cider vinegar

entries: Freshly ground black pepper

entries.entry: {=amount1/c} garlic clove, pressed or grated (about {=amount2/v} teaspoon)
{=amount1/v} large red bell pepper, membranes and seeds removed, cut into thin strips
{=amount1/v} jar pickled beans/vine blight, drained and halved (about {=amount2/v} cups)
{=amount1/v} cup lightly packed, torn fresh parsley

instructions.name: Pickle the beans:
entries: Fill a large bowl with ice water and set aside. In a large saucepan over high heat, bring 3 quarts of water to a rapid boil. Add 2 teaspoons of salt and the green beans and cook until bright green and barely tender, about 3 minutes. Drain the beans and immediately transfer them to the ice water to stop the cooking (keep the saucepan handy). Once the beans are cool, drain and dry them and set aside.

Add 2 cups of water, the vinegar, 2½ tablespoons of salt, sugar, peppercorns, mustard seeds, celery seed, and red pepper flakes (if using) to the saucepan. Return it to medium-high heat and bring to a strong simmer, stirring to dissolve the salt and sugar.

Pack an equal portion of the beans, 2 garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves, and 2 whole cloves into each of three 1-pint mason jars. Pour an equal portion of the hot liquid mixture into each jar to cover the beans, cool to room temperature, screw on the lids, and refrigerate for at least 48 hours and up to 4 weeks before serving.

instructions.name: Make the salad:
entries: In a colander or large strainer set over a medium bowl, toss the cabbage with 2 teaspoons of salt and set aside at room temperature until the cabbage wilts slightly, at least 1 hour and up to 4 hours. Rinse the cabbage well under very cold running water, drain thoroughly, and dry very well with a clean kitchen towel or paper towels. Scrape the cabbage into a large bowl and fluff it with your fingers.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, cover the shallots with very cold water and set aside to soak for about 15 minutes. Drain the shallots and dry well with paper towels.

In a large salad bowl, whisk the bean brine, vinegar, ¼ teaspoon of salt, ¾ teaspoon of black pepper, garlic, and mustard to incorporate. Vigorously whisk in the olive oil to blend. Adjust the seasoning if necessary. Add the cabbage, shallots, red pepper, pickled green beans, and parsley to the bowl and toss to combine. Adjust the seasoning if necessary, and serve.

recipe.name: Pieglass

instructions.name: To make the pumpkin pie syrup:
entries: In a small saucepan, cook the pumpkin puree over low heat for about 3 minutes, stirring constantly until thickened and slightly darker in color. Add the pumpkin pie spice, granulated sugar, water, and vanilla and stir to combine. Increase the heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally. Simmer for 2 minutes and remove from the heat. Set a fine-mesh strainer over a heatproof container and pour the syrup through to remove the solids, stirring with a rubber spatula if necessary to drain. Let the syrup cool completely before using. Store any remaining pumpkin pie syrup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

instructions: In a medium bowl, combine the heavy cream and confectioners' sugar. Using an electric hand mixer or whisk, beat the mixture until soft peaks form. Pour 12 ounces of cider into each of two pint glasses. Add ½ cup of ice cream to each glass, being careful not to overfill. Top each glass with a dollop of whipped cream and drizzle with 2 tablespoons of pumpkin pie syrup. Serve at once.

recipe.name: Plate of Silver

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds small (2-inch) red-skinned or Yukon gold creamer potatoes, scrubbed

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: About {=amount1/v} ounces white anchovy fillets or boquerónes (see Cook's Note)

instructions: With a rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F. Spread the potatoes on a baking sheet and roast until they are very tender, about 35 minutes. Remove the pan from the oven (leave the oven on) and set the potatoes aside to cool for about 10 minutes.

When the potatoes are cool enough to handle, transfer to a large bowl. Brush the same baking sheet with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper. Return the potatoes to the baking sheet, spaced about 2½ inches apart. With another baking sheet or the bottom of a mug or a potato masher, sharply press down on the potatoes to break their skins and compress the flesh until about ¾ inch thick. Brush the potatoes with the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil and sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper. Return the potatoes to the oven and roast until deep golden brown, about 25 minutes longer, turning the baking sheet halfway through. Taste a small piece of a potato and adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary.
Arrange the potatoes on a serving platter, lay an anchovy fillet over each one, and sprinkle with the parsley. Serve immediately.
noteCook: Meaty marinated white anchovies are popular in Spain, where they're called boquerónes. Instead of being packed in oil or salt, the anchovies are marinated in vinegar, which gives them a piquant flavor and whitens the flesh. They're less salty and intense than their tinned, oil-packed brethren.
Using a second baking sheet will smash all the potatoes at once, whereas if you use the bottom of a mug or a potato masher, you will have to smash them individually.

recipe.name: Plate-of-Gold

ingredients.name: Sweet and Sour Sauce

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} cup apricot or peach jam or orange marmalade
{=amount1/v} tablespoon light or dark brown sugar

entries: Kosher salt

ingredients.name: Tempura

entries.entry: About {=amount1/v} quarts canola or other high-smoke-point oil for frying

entries: Kosher salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} cup plus {=amount2/v} tablespoon sparkling water, cold
{=amount1/v} ounces fresh shiitake mushrooms, stemmed, very large caps halved, cold
{=amount1/v} sweet potato, peeled, halved lengthwise, and cut crosswise into {=amount2/v}-inch slices, cold
{=amount1/v} yellow onion, trimmed, halved pole to pole, and cut lengthwise into {=amount2/v}-inch slivers, cold

instructions: MAKE THE SAUCE. In a small saucepan over medium heat, warm the jam, stirring, until mostly fluid, 3 to 5 minutes. Add the ketchup, vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, chile-garlic sauce (if using), and ½ teaspoon salt and whisk to combine. Bring to a simmer and cook, whisking, to blend the flavors, about 1 minute. Set aside to cool to room temperature. Taste and adjust the seasoning with additional salt, if necessary.

MAKE THE TEMPURA. Line a large, rimmed baking sheet with a double layer of paper towels and set aside. Clip a deep-fry or candy thermometer to the side of a heavy 5-quart Dutch oven, add the oil, and warm over medium-high heat to 390°F. Preheat the oven to 200°F. Place a wire rack on a second large, rimmed baking sheet and set aside.

Meanwhile, fill a large bowl about one-third full with ice and about 1½ cups water. In a medium (preferably stainless-steel) bowl that will fit in the larger bowl, whisk together the cake and all-purpose flours and ¾ teaspoon salt; set this bowl in the bowl with the ice water to chill the flour mixture. When the oil reaches 390°F, add the sparkling water to the flour mixture and stir just until the wet and dry are incorporated, but still a little lumpy; do not overmix.

Working with about eight pieces at a time, use tongs or chopsticks to dip them in the batter to coat thoroughly. Allow any excess batter to drip off, then slip them into the oil and fry until slightly puffed and pale gold, adjusting the heat as necessary to maintain 390°F, stirring to prevent sticking, and turning the pieces over in the oil once or twice to promote even frying, 5 to 6 minutes for each batch. With a spider skimmer, slotted spoon, or long tongs, transfer the tempura to the paper towel-lined baking sheet to drain for about 30 seconds. Sprinkle lightly with salt and place on the wire rack set on the baking sheet and put in the oven to keep warm. Allow the oil to recover to 390°F and fry the remaining batches. Serve with the sweet and sour sauce.

recipe.name: Poetess
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes

instructions.name: To make the lavender syrup:
entries: In a small saucepan, combine the water and sugar. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, add the lavender, and stir to combine. Remove from the heat and let steep for 5 minutes. Strain the mixture into a fine-mesh strainer or cheesecloth over a cup with a spout to remove the solids and set aside. In a separate cup, stir together the hot water and butterfly pea powder until no clumps remain. Add to the lavender syrup and mix well. Allow to fully cool before using. Store any remaining lavender syrup in an airtight jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

instructions: In a mixing glass, add the tequila, vermouth, and ½ ounce of lavender syrup. Fill the glass halfway with ice and stir with a long-handled spoon to chill, about 30 seconds. Add a large ice cube to two rocks glasses. Strain and divide the mixture evenly between the two glasses. Top with lemon juice, lavender sprigs, and lemon peel. Watch the color change with the addition of acid, and serve at once.

recipe.name: Potato Leek Soup

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} leeks, white and light green parts, thinly sliced
{=amount1/v} pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cut into {=amount2/v}-inch pieces

instructions: In a large heavy pot over medium heat, fry the bacon, turning it over as necessary, until well-rendered and lightly browned, about 13 minutes. Use a slotted spoon or tongs to transfer the bacon to a paper towel.

Add the leeks, celery, and thyme to the pot and cook, stirring, until the vegetables soften, about 5 minutes. Add the potatoes, broth, and 1 teaspoon salt. Simmer until the potatoes are soft, 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove the soup from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend until smooth. Alternatively, blend the soup in batches using a countertop blender.

Return the soup to the pot over medium heat. Stir in the cream and simmer until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Taste and season with black pepper and more salt, if needed. Crumble the cooked bacon. Serve each bowl of soup piping hot and topped with bacon (alternatively, the soup can be served cold).

recipe.name: Potion of Restoration
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes
instructions: In a cocktail shaker, muddle together 11 of the blackberries, the sugar, and lemon juice until the sugar dissolves fully. Add the gin and butterfly pea powder (if using). Fill the shaker about halfway with ice. Cover and shake to blend and chill, 30 seconds. Fill two chilled old-fashion or rocks glasses about halfway with ice and strain half the mixture into each, then pour ½ ounce crème de mure over the ice in each. Run one lemon twist around the rim of each glass and drop it in; add two of the remaining blackberries to each glass and serve at once.
noteCook: The drinks have a purple hue from the muddled blackberries, but to make the color extra vibrant, use the butterfly pea powder, which creates a vivid magenta color in the presence of an acid, such as lemon juice. Butterfly pea powder is available online and at some natural foods stores with a good selection of herbs and spices.
Crème de mure is a blackberry liqueur. If you can't find it, crème de cassis, a black currant liqueur, is a fine substitute.

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoon unsalted butter, at cool room temperature, cut into small pieces

ingredients.name: BREAD
entries: Table salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} cup neutral oil (such as avocado, safflower, sunflower, grapeseed, or canola)
{=amount1/v} cup lightly packed light brown sugar
{=amount1/v} cup porter, stout, or oatmeal stout

instructions.name: Make the topping:
entries: In a medium bowl, combine the brown sugar, flour, cinnamon, ginger, and salt. Add the butter and, using your fingers, work it into the dry mixture until the mixture resembles wet sand. Refrigerate until ready to use.

instructions.name: Make the bread:
entries: In a medium nonstick skillet over medium heat, cook the pumpkin, constantly stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan with a heatproof flexible spatula, until slightly thickened and a shade darker, 10 to 12 minutes. Add the cinnamon, allspice, and ¼ teaspoon of salt and stir to incorporate. Spread the mixture on a plate and cool it to room temperature, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray a 9 by 5-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking spray and set aside.

In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and 1 teaspoon of salt to combine. In a large bowl, whisk the cooled pumpkin, oil, brown sugar, honey, and eggs until uniform. Add the beer and whisk to incorporate. Add the dry mixture and, using a flexible spatula, fold to blend the wet and dry ingredients just until no pockets of dry ingredients remain (do not overmix). Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top. Sprinkle the chilled topping mixture evenly over the surface, breaking it into small pieces as you go.

Bake until the edges pull away from the pan and a toothpick inserted into the center of the loaf comes out clean, about 45 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through the baking time. Transfer the pan to a wire rack and cool for about 20 minutes. Turn the loaf out of the pan, place it right side up onto the rack, cool to room temperature, and serve.

recipe.name: Purple Grapemash No. 3

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ounce fresh lime juice, plus 2 lime slices

instructions: Chill two sturdy wine glasses, stemmed or not, or margarita glasses.

In a blender, combine the rum, lime juice, grape jelly, and ice cubes and blend until the ice is finely crushed and the mixture is uniform, slushy, and moves easily in the blender jar (the timing will depend on the power of your blender). Divide the mixture between the prepared glasses, garnish each with a lime slice, and serve immediately, with straws, if desired.
noteCook: To chill a sturdy wine glass, put it in the freezer for an hour before using.

recipe.name: Purskul Welcome Soup

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ounces thick-cut bacon (about {=amount2/v} or {=amount2/v} slices), cut crosswise into ½-inch pieces
{=amount1/v} large celery ribs, trimmed and chopped
{=amount1/c} garlic cloves, pressed or grated (about {=amount2/v} teaspoons)
{=amount1/xt} 15-ounce cans cannellini, white kidney, great Northern, or navy beans, drained but not rinsed

instructions: Line a plate with paper towels and set aside.

In a large, heavy pot over medium heat, cook the bacon, stirring frequently, until rendered and lightly browned, about 14 minutes. With a slotted spoon, transfer the bacon to the prepared plate to drain and reserve. Pour off all but 1½ tablespoons of the bacon fat.

Return the pot to medium heat and add the onion, carrots, celery, bay leaves, thyme, and ½ teaspoon of salt. Cook, stirring, until the vegetables begin to soften, about 4 minutes. Adjust the heat to medium-low, cover, and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have released their juices, about 4 minutes longer.

Adjust the heat to medium, clear the center of the pot, add the tomato paste, and cook in the clearing, stirring, until sticky and starting to darken, about 2 minutes. Stir the paste and vegetables together. Add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Add the chicken broth, raise the heat to medium-high, and bring to a boil. Adjust the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes longer. Remove the bay leaves.

In the carafe of a blender, purée half the beans (about 2 cups) with 2 cups of the hot liquid mixture until smooth. Add the puréed mixture, the remaining beans, 1½ teaspoons of salt, and pepper to taste to the pot. Adjust the heat to medium and bring to a simmer. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the flavors are melded and the whole beans are heated through, about 10 minutes longer. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper as necessary. Add most of the parsley (reserving a little for garnish) and stir to mix. Ladle into individual bowls, sprinkle with some of the reserved bacon and remaining parsley, and serve.

recipe.name: Qualinesti Vegetable Stew

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} Japanese or Chinese eggplant, sliced {=amount2/v} inch thick

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the middle of the oven.

In a 12-inch ovenproof skillet over medium heat, combine ¼ cup of the olive oil, half the garlic, and the thyme and cook, stirring, until fragrant and the garlic just begins to sizzle, 1 to 2 minutes. Scrape the mixture into a small bowl and set aside.

Add the remaining oil to the skillet over medium heat and allow the oil to warm until shimmering. Add the onion and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the tomato puree, sugar, and pepper to taste. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 7 minutes. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt, if necessary, and set aside off the heat to cool slightly. Add 2 tablespoons of the basil and stir to mix; spread and smooth the mixture into an even layer in the skillet.

Working in concentric circles from the edges of the skillet toward the middle, neatly shingle the sliced zucchini, yellow squash, eggplant, and tomatoes, alternating and overlapping the vegetables and packing them tightly in a single layer. Drizzle the reserved garlic-thyme oil evenly over the vegetables and sprinkle with about ¾ teaspoon salt and ¾ teaspoon pepper. Cover the skillet and bake until the vegetables begin to soften, about 30 minutes. Remove the cover and continue baking until the vegetables are very tender and bubbling around the edges of the skillet, about 20 minutes more.
Rest the dish for 10 minutes, sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons basil and serve.
noteCook: Japanese and Chinese eggplants are long and slender, with a diameter similar to that of zucchini or the fat end of yellow squash. If you use globe eggplant instead, choose the skinniest one you can find and cut the slices to a similar size as the squashes and tomatoes. Make sure the curved side faces out when you arrange them in the skillet.

recipe.name: Quij's Plate

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pound fresh sausage (your choice of flavor), casings removed
{=amount1/v} pounds red or all-purpose potatoes, cut into ½-inch cubes
{=amount1/v} large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped
{=amount1/v} tablespoon chopped fresh sage, or 2 teaspoons minced fresh thyme or rosemary

instructions: In a large skillet (preferably cast iron) over medium heat, warm 1 tablespoon of the neutral oil until shimmering. Add the sausage and cook, stirring and breaking it into small pieces, until it no longer appears raw, 3 to 4 minutes. With a slotted spoon, transfer the sausage to a bowl or plate, leaving behind the rendered fat.

In the same skillet over medium heat, warm the remaining 2 tablespoons neutral oil with the sausage fat until shimmering. Add the potatoes and ¼ teaspoon salt and stir to coat the potatoes with the oil and fat. Add the water, cover, and cook until the potatoes are just tender, 12 to 14 minutes. Uncover the skillet; add the onions, bell pepper, and ½ teaspoon salt; and cook, stirring frequently, until softened and light golden, about 8 minutes. Add the sage and garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Add the half-and-half, 1 teaspoon salt, and black pepper to taste, stirring until well blended. Pat the mixture flat in the pan, adjust the heat to medium-high, and cook, undisturbed, until the visible moisture evaporates, there is no more visible bubbling on the surface, and the bottom begins to brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Using a wooden spoon or a stiff spatula, stir the mixture, scraping the brown bits from the bottom of the pan. Return the sausage to the pan and add most of the parsley, stirring to blend. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary.

Using the back of a spoon, make an indentation for each egg, crack an egg into each, and sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper. Cover the skillet, adjust the heat to medium, and cook until the egg whites are set and the yolks are warm and slightly thickened but still liquid, 6 to 9 minutes, depending on how firm you like your eggs. Sprinkle with the remaining parsley before serving.

recipe.name: Quith-pa

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ounces ({=amount2/v} cup) dried apricots, coarsely chopped

instructions: Using a Microplane, grate the orange peel to yield 1½ teaspoons of finely grated zest. Squeeze the orange to yield 1½ tablespoons of juice.

In a full-size or mini food processor, combine the apricots, ¼ cup of the coconut, the orange zest and juice, vanilla, and a tiny pinch of salt. Process until the mixture is very finely chopped, uniform, and cohesive, pulsing and stopping to scrape down the sides of the work bowl as necessary. Scrape the mixture into a small bowl. Put the remaining ½ cup coconut in a wide, shallow bowl.

Roll scant 1-tablespoon portions of the apricot mixture into 1-inch balls, gently pressing as you roll to help them cohere (you should have 15 or 16 balls). Working with three or four balls at a time, roll them in the remaining coconut, pressing them gently to help the coconut adhere. Place the balls on a plate and rest them (to firm up and dry out slightly) for 45 minutes. The balls will keep, stored in an airtight container at room temperature, for about 3 days.

recipe.name: Ray of Frost
instructions: Chill two cocktail glasses, martini glasses, or coupes ({@recipe Tika's Honey Mead|HFFotM|see Cook's Note, this page}). Fill a large mixing glass about halfway with ice and add the gin, absinthe, and vermouth. Stir to blend and chill, about 30 seconds. Strain between the two chilled glasses. Run a lemon twist around the rim of each glass and drop it in before serving.

entries.name: TIP:
entries: To chill a cocktail or martini glass or a coupe, put it in the freezer for an hour before using.

recipe.name: Red Larch Crumblecakes
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} bunches scallions (about {=amount2/c} slender scallions), whites and greens thinly sliced (about {=amount1/v} cups)
{=amount1/v} medium-large carrot, peeled and coarsely grated (about {=amount2/v} cup)
{=amount1/v} pound thick-sliced deli turkey or sliced roast turkey, neatly diced into roughly ½-inch pieces (about {=amount2/v} cup)
{=amount1/v} cup plain low-fat or whole yogurt

instructions: In a strainer, rinse the chickpeas well and drain for 10 minutes. Line a microwave-safe plate with a double layer of paper towels. Spread the chickpeas on the lined plate in a single layer and sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper. Microwave until the chickpeas appear drier and some have split at the seams, about 6 minutes; set aside to cool.

With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray a 9-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking spray. In a large bowl, whisk the flours, baking powder, paprika, onion powder, cayenne pepper, 1½ teaspoons of salt, and 1 teaspoon of black pepper to combine. Add the scallions, carrot, turkey, and chickpeas, toss to distribute, and make a well in the center.

In a medium bowl, beat the eggs. Add the yogurt and oil and whisk vigorously until blended and uniform. Pour the egg mixture into the dry ingredients and, with a large flexible spatula, stir and fold until just incorporated (do not overmix).

Scrape the batter into the prepared loaf pan, work it into the corners, smooth the top, and bake until golden brown and a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean, 55 to 60 minutes, rotating the pan and brushing the top with the melted butter halfway through (do not overbake). On a wire rack, cool the loaf for about 20 minutes. Remove the loaf from the pan, return it to the rack, cool to room temperature, slice with a serrated knife, and serve.
noteCook: If you don't have chickpea flour, you can use all-purpose flour instead and the crumblecake will come out just fine.

recipe.name: Reghed Venison Pot Roast

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds beef chuck roast, trimmed of excess fat

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons neutral-tasting oil, such as vegetable, canola, safflower, or grapeseed
{=amount1/v} cup lightly packed dried apricots; {=amount2/v} cup finely chopped, {=amount3/v} cup halved
{=amount1/v} whole head garlic, outermost papery skins removed, top one-quarter of the head cut off to expose the cloves
{=amount1/v} ounces carrots, peeled and cut into {=amount2/v}-inch pieces
{=amount1/v} ounces Yukon gold potatoes, scrubbed or peeled, halved lengthwise, and halves cut into {=amount2/v}-inch pieces

instructions: Dry the beef with paper towels, tie it into a uniform shape with kitchen twine at 2-inch intervals, and sprinkle generously with salt and pepper.

In a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat, warm 1 tablespoon of the oil until shimmering. Add the beef and cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned on the bottom, 3 to 4 minutes. Turn the beef a quarter turn and continue cooking, until well browned on each of the remaining three sides, about 10 minutes more; adjust the heat if the bottom of the pot threatens to burn. Transfer the beef to a large bowl.

Return the pot to medium-high heat, add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, and allow it to warm until shimmering. Add the onion, bay leaves, and 1 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pot occasionally, until the onion begins to soften and releases some liquid, about 4 minutes. Add the paprika and flour and continue to cook, stirring, for 2 minutes more. Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute more.
Add the wine to the pot and stir and scrape the bottom to loosen and dissolve the browned bits. Add the broth, finely chopped apricots, garlic, thyme, and ½ teaspoon salt and stir.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 300°F with a rack in the lower-middle of the oven.

Nestle the beef (and any accumulated juices) into the pot (the liquid should come about halfway up the sides of the meat). Cover the pot, transfer it to the oven, and cook for 1¾ hours. Then add the carrots, potatoes, and halved apricots, nestling them into the liquid. Cover the pot, return to the oven, and continue to cook until the beef is extremely tender (a paring knife should slip easily into the meat) and it registers 200°F on an instant-read thermometer, 2¼ to 2¾ hours more.

Transfer the beef to a cutting board and, using a large slotted spoon, spoon the carrots, potatoes, onion, and apricot halves to a serving platter; tent loosely with foil to keep warm. Pour the accumulated liquid into a fat separator or measuring cup; remove and discard the bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Reserve the garlic. Let the liquid rest until the fat rises to the surface, about 10 minutes. If using a fat separator, pour the liquid into another container; if using a measuring cup, tilt it and use a wide, shallow soup spoon to skim fat off the surface and discard it (the liquid will be thick, and there may not be much fat at the surface.)

Meanwhile, squeeze the cooked garlic cloves from their skins and mash them to a paste with a fork. Stir the garlic and most of the parsley into the defatted liquid. Taste the gravy and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper, if necessary.

Remove the twine from the beef and cut it against the grain into ½-inch-thick slices (or pull it apart into pieces) and sprinkle it very lightly with salt and pepper. Place the meat on the platter with the vegetables and apricots, pour the gravy over the meat, sprinkle with the remaining parsley, and serve.

recipe.name: Restoration
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes
instructions: In a large pitcher, combine the coconut water, coconut milk, lemon juice, and honey. Using a long-handled spoon, stir well until the honey is dissolved. Add the lemon slices. Fill the pitcher halfway with ice and serve in highball glasses at once.
noteCook: Make sure to shake or stir the coconut milk smooth before adding it to the pitcher. Canned coconut milk tends to separate due to its fat content. It will be easier to incorporate into the final beverage if it's already homogenous.

recipe.name: Rewards

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} ounces rhubarb, trimmed and sliced ¼ inch thick
{=amount1/v} ounces fresh strawberries, hulled, halved, and sliced ¼ inch thick

instructions: On a gently floured surface, lay down the sheet of puff pastry. Roll the pastry out to ⅛-inch thickness and use a quart container or a bowl with a roughly 5½-inch diameter to cut out 6 circles. Transfer the circles into the cups of a muffin tin, gently pushing down the bottom and crimping the sides to fit.

In a medium bowl, gently stir the rhubarb, strawberries, sugar, vanilla extract, cornstarch, lemon juice, and salt to combine. Using a ¼-cup measure, scoop the filling into the muffin cups. Brush the exposed edges of puff pastry with egg wash and place the tarts into the freezer to chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Bake the tarts for 25 minutes, until the edges are golden and the filling is bubbling. Place on a wire rack and let cool before serving.

recipe.name: Rime Of The Frostmaiden
instructions: Pour the bottle of wine into a 13 × 9-inch pan or in two ice cube trays. Place the wine-filled pan into the freezer and let it chill for 6 hours, until mostly solid. Scrape the frozen wine into a blender jar. Add the blueberries, blue curaçao, lemon juice, and agave syrup and blend until smooth. Transfer the blender jar to the freezer to chill for 30 minutes, until the mixture has thickened. Return the blender jar to its base and pulse the mixture a few times to loosen it. Pour into champagne coupes and serve at once.
noteCook: Using frozen blueberries will help keep your mixture cool despite the heat generated by the blender. It also increases the intensity of the berries' natural coloring.

recipe.name: River Fish Fry
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Line a plate with paper towels and set aside. In a small bowl, mix 1 teaspoon each of salt and pepper. Sprinkle the fish fillets evenly with the salt and pepper mixture and rest at room temperature until they appear slightly moist and glossy, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a wide, shallow dish (such as a pie plate), gently whisk the cornmeal, paprika, thyme, oregano, onion powder, celery seed, and 1 teaspoon each of salt and pepper to combine.

In a large (12-inch) skillet over medium heat, warm the oil until shimmering. Dredge the fish fillets in the cornmeal mixture, gently patting to help it adhere. Gently add the fillets to the oil and cook, undisturbed, until golden brown on the bottom, 3 to 4 minutes (there should be active, but not violent, bubbling at the edges of the fillets). Carefully flip the fillets and cook, undisturbed, until the second side is golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes (the thicker ends of the fillets should register about 135ºF on an instant-read thermometer). Carefully transfer the fillets to the prepared plate, rest for 3 minutes, and serve with lemon wedges.
noteCook: If you use tilapia instead of catfish, trim off the very thin part of the fillets and cook them slightly less than the thicker portions.
Instead of your own spices, you can use Old Bay or another seafood seasoning mix, or a favorite premixed seasoning blend such as Cajun.

recipe.name: Roast Gammon Pie

ingredients.entry: Pastry for a double-crust pie (about {=amount1/v} pounds), thawed and rested at room temperature until pliable without cracking, about 30 minutes
{=amount1/v} pound frozen pearl onions (about {=amount2/v} cups), thawed and blotted dry with paper towel
{=amount1/v} medium leek (white and light green parts), halved lengthwise and thinly sliced (about {=amount2/v} cups)
{=amount1/v} medium-small sweet potato (about {=amount2/v} ounces), peeled and cut into ½-inch pieces (about {=amount3/v} cups)
{=amount1/v} pounds ham steak, cut into ¾-inch cubes (about {=amount2/v} cups)

instructions: On a floured work surface or sheet of parchment paper, roll out one piece of pastry into a 12-inch circle, if necessary (see Cook's Note). Loosely roll the pastry around the rolling pin and gently transfer it into a deep-dish pie plate. Use one hand to gently lift the edge of the pastry and use the other hand to lightly press the pastry into the plate bottom and up the sides, leaving an overhang of about 1 inch. Set aside.

Again on a floured work surface or sheet of parchment paper, roll the second piece of pastry into a 12-inch circle, if necessary. Transfer it to a parchment-lined baking sheet or large plate. Loosely cover both it and the pastry in the pie plate with plastic wrap and refrigerate both pastries until they are firm, at least 30 minutes.
With the rack in the low position, preheat the oven to 450°F. Place a rimmed baking sheet on the rack to preheat while making the filling.

In a large, straight-sided sauté pan over medium-high heat, warm the olive oil until shimmering. Add the pearl onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until their liquid has evaporated and they are dry and lightly browned, about 3 minutes. Transfer them to a bowl and set aside.

Return the sauté pan to medium heat, add the butter and allow it to melt, swirling to coat the pan. Add the leek and ½ teaspoon of salt and cook, stirring, until softened, about 3 minutes. Add the thyme, ginger, allspice, and ½ teaspoon of pepper and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 1½ minutes. Continuing to stir constantly, gradually add the broth and then the half-and-half, in a slow, steady stream. Adjust the heat to medium-high, bring to a strong simmer, and cook, stirring, until smooth and thick, about 1 minute. Add the sweet potato, adjust the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until nearly tender, about 8 minutes. Add the brandy and mustard and cook, stirring to incorporate, for about 1½ minutes. Off heat, add the reserved pearl onions, ham, and parsley and stir to distribute. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary.

Scrape the filling into the pastry-lined pie plate and spread it evenly. Loosely roll the remaining dough round around the rolling pin and gently unroll it over the filling, leaving an overhang of about 1 inch. Using kitchen shears, cut evenly through both layers of overhanging pastry, leaving an overhang of about ½ inch. Fold the pastry under itself so that the edge of the fold is even with the edge of the pie plate, and flute the pastry using your thumb and forefinger or crimp it with the tines of a fork to seal.

In a small bowl, beat the egg with 1 tablespoon of water and brush onto the top of the pie (you'll probably have some left over). Cut a couple of roughly 2-inch slits near the center of the pastry (to vent steam as the pie bakes), set the pie on the preheated baking sheet, and bake until the top is light golden brown, about 20 minutes. Adjust the temperature to 375°F, rotate the baking sheet, and continue baking until the crust is deeply browned and the filling is bubbling around the edges, about 15 minutes. Transfer the pie, still in the pie plate, onto a wire rack, cool it for at least 40 minutes, and serve.
noteCook: Some frozen pastry is sold rolled up in small packages, so you'll have to unroll the thawed pastry, and depending on the dimensions, use a rolling pin to roll it into a circle large enough to fit into the pie plate. Sometimes, though, you can find pastry that's already sized into circles that will fit into a pie plate, sold flat in large square boxes.

recipe.name: Roasted Plums and Burrata

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} medium dark plums (about 2½ inches), halved and pitted (or quartered if large) (see Cook's Notes)
{=amount1/v} tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} 4-ounce balls burrata, at room temperature (see Cook's Notes)

instructions: With a rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F.

In a large (at least 12-inch), ovenproof skillet, gently toss the plums and 1½ tablespoons of the oil to coat. Sprinkle the brown sugar over the plums, gently toss again to distribute, and turn the plums cut-sides down. Set the skillet over medium-high heat and cook the plums, undisturbed, until the cut sides are caramelized, 3 to 4 minutes.

Off heat, turn the plums cut-sides up, sprinkle very lightly with salt and pepper, the shallot, and thyme, and drizzle with the remaining 1½ tablespoons of oil. Roast until the plums are tender and the skins loosen, 4 to 5 minutes. Remove the skillet from the oven and allow the plums to cool to warm or room temperature.

Place the burrata balls on a serving dish and cut them open to expose the creamy centers. Drizzle lightly with honey and olive oil and sprinkle very lightly with salt and pepper. Arrange the plums around the burrata, sprinkle the parsley and fennel (if using) over the plums and cheese, and serve.
noteCook: Choose plums that are a day or two from perfectly ripe, as they stand up to the heat better than really ripe fruit.
If you can't get burrata, lightly seasoned ricotta or room-temperature mascarpone is also good.

recipe.name: Rollrum

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} large mint leaves, plus {=amount2/v} sprigs for garnish

ingredients: Small ice cubes or coarsely crushed ice
instructions: In a cocktail shaker, muddle the sugar and water until the sugar dissolves and the liquid is syrupy. Add the mint leaves and muddle gently to bruise them and release their fragrance (do not pulverize). Fill the shaker about halfway with ice and add the absinthe. Cover and shake to blend and chill, 30 seconds. Fill two chilled old-fashioned, rocks, or small Collins glasses about halfway with ice and divide the mixture between them. If using, add half the seltzer to each and stir gently to blend. Holding the mint sprigs by their stems, slap them against the back of your hand or forearm (to help release their fragrance), garnish each glass with a sprig, and serve at once.
noteCook: Although less potent in terms of alcohol content, you can substitute other anise-flavored liqueurs, such as pastis, Pernod, Herbsaint, or even ouzo, for the absinthe.

entries.name: TIP:
entries: To chill an old-fashioned, rocks, or Collins glass, put it in the freezer for an hour before using.

recipe.name: Root Vegetables, Gratin-Style

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/c} garlic cloves, {=amount2/c} smashed and {=amount3/c} very thinly sliced
{=amount1/v} tablespoons unsalted butter, {=amount2/v} tablespoon softened, for the baking dish, and {=amount3/v} tablespoons melted
{=amount1/v} pounds purple potatoes, peeled and sliced very thin (about ¼ inch) (see Cook's Notes)
{=amount1/v} pounds yellow turnip or rutabaga, peeled and sliced very thin (about ¼ inch)
{=amount1/v} pounds golden beets, peeled and sliced very thin (about ¼ inch) (see Cook's Notes)
{=amount1/v} tablespoon minced fresh thyme or rosemary

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} medium shallots, peeled and halved lengthwise
{=amount1/v} tablespoon finely chopped fresh parsley or chives, for garnish

instructions: With the rack in the upper-middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F. Rub the inside of a medium (2-quart) shallow baking or gratin dish with the smashed garlic clove, mashing it as you go so little bits of it stick to the dish. Allow the garlic to dry for 2 to 3 minutes and butter the dish with the softened butter.

Put the potatoes, turnips, and beets each into their own separate bowls. To each, add 1 tablespoon of the melted butter and toss to coat. Add 1 teaspoon of the thyme, ½ teaspoon of salt, pepper to taste, one-third of the sliced garlic, and 3 tablespoons of the grated Parmesan to each bowl and toss to coat the vegetables well.

Arrange small bunches of the sliced vegetables in the prepared dish, standing them up in a pattern of your choice (concentric circles or bias-tilted rows, for instance), alternating them by color attractively and packing them very tightly.

With a flexible spatula, scrape the residual butter from the now-empty bowls and re-melt it. In one of the now-empty bowls, toss the shallots and the re-melted butter, and tuck them into the dish with the vegetables, distributing them evenly.
Drizzle the oil evenly over the vegetables. Tightly cover the dish with foil, place it on a baking sheet, and bake until the vegetables are softened but not yet fully tender, about 45 minutes.

Remove the foil, sprinkle the remaining 3 tablespoons of Parmesan evenly over the vegetables, and continue baking until the vegetables are well browned and very tender, 25 to 30 minutes longer. Rest the gratin for at least 10 minutes, sprinkle the parsley evenly over it, and serve.
noteCook: A mandoline or other slicer makes quick work of thinly slicing the root vegetables.

If you can't get purple potatoes, either Yukon gold or all-purpose white-flesh potatoes will work, though the dish will obviously be less colorful. Another option would be to use red beets in place of the golden ones, though red beets are messier to work with.

recipe.name: Rothé Steak

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/xt} 1-pound boneless strip steaks (see Cook's Note), 1½ to 2 inches thick

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} large sprigs fresh thyme or rosemary

instructions: Using paper towels, pat the steaks dry and season generously with salt and pepper on both sides and along the edges. Place the steaks on a plate and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour. (Or refrigerate, loosely covered, for up to 2 days. Return the steaks to room temperature before cooking.)

Set a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat for 7 minutes (the pan may smoke a bit). Adjust the heat to high, add the neutral oil, and swirl to coat the bottom of the pan (the oil will smoke too). Add the steaks and cook, flipping them every 30 seconds, until a pale golden crust begins to form on both sides, 3 to 4 minutes.

Adjust the heat to medium-high, slide the steaks to one side of the skillet, add the butter to the other side, and allow it to melt and foam slightly. Add the garlic and thyme to the butter. Tilt the pan toward the butter so that it pools opposite the steaks and, while continuing to flip the steaks every 30 seconds, use a long-handled, large metal spoon to baste them with the butter and aromatics, concentrating on spots that are lighter and less crusted. (If the butter smokes or the steaks begin to burn, lower the heat slightly.) Cook, basting and flipping the steaks, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest spot registers 120° to 125°F for medium-rare, about 7 minutes longer, or about 130°F for medium, 8 to 9 minutes longer.
Transfer the steaks to a carving board, tent loosely with aluminum foil, and let rest for 10 minutes. Slice the steaks against the grain into roughly ½-inch-thick slices before serving.
noteCook: Cast iron is the skillet of choice here because it retains heat so well.

This cooking technique is a bit messy—the fat splatters in the intense heat, and a splatter screen is of no help because of the frequent turning. The entire process moves fast, so turn on your exhaust fan and have your tongs, basting spoon, and thermometer at hand before you start cooking. And, of course, use oven mitts when handling the screaming-hot skillet.

Depending on where you live, strip steak may be called shell steak, sirloin strip steak, New York strip steak, Kansas City strip steak, or Texas strip steak, among other names. Whatever name it goes by, make sure it's thick.
A large-flake, crunchy salt, like Maldon, is a terrific finish at serving time.

recipe.name: Ruby Cordial
instructions: Fill two small rocks or old-fashioned glasses about halfway with ice. Fill a large cocktail shaker about halfway with ice and add the port, brandy, lemon juice, and grenadine. Cover and shake to blend and chill, about 30 seconds. Strain the mixture into each glass. Run a lemon twist around the rim of each glass, drop it in, and garnish with a cherry before serving.

recipe.name: Rumtack
instructions: With a rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray a 10- to 12-cup Bundt pan with nonstick cooking spray and dust generously with flour.

instructions.name: To make the cake:
entries: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt and set aside.

In a large saucepan over medium heat, warm the butter and the ginger beer for 3 to 5 minutes, until the butter is melted. Remove from the heat and add the cocoa powder, sugar, cinnamon, allspice, cardamom, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg. Stir to combine. Add the rum, vanilla, buttermilk, and eggs and stir until the eggs are fully incorporated. Carefully add the butter mixture to the flour mixture and stir well with a rubber spatula until no flour streaks remain. Pour the batter into the prepared Bundt pan. Bake until a cake tester or toothpick inserted in the thickest part of the cake is removed with a few moist crumbs, 50 to 60 minutes.

instructions.name: To make the glaze:
entries: In a small saucepan, combine the butter, sugar, and rum. Set the saucepan over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally until the mixture comes to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened and glossy. Remove from the heat.

instructions: Remove the cake from the oven and transfer to a wire rack. Using a skewer, poke holes all over the cake, stopping three-quarters of the way into the cake's interior. Spoon half of the glaze over the holes and cool for 30 minutes. Spoon another quarter of the glaze over the cake and let soak for another 30 minutes. Place a serving plate on top of the Bundt pan and invert to turn the cake out, tapping the sides of the pan if necessary to release the cake. Warm the glaze over low heat if necessary to loosen it up and brush the remaining glaze over the top of the cake. Slice and serve. Store the cake covered in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

recipe.name: Saerloonian Glowfire

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} sugar cubes, or 2 teaspoons granulated sugar
{=amount1/v} ounces Prosecco or other sparkling wine, cold

instructions: Put a sugar cube in the bottoms of two champagne flutes. Pour ½ ounce port and ½ ounce Poire Williams into each flute and swirl to begin dissolving the sugar. Slowly add 3 ounces Prosecco to each one, and garnish with a slice of pear. Serve immediately.

recipe.name: Salbread

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons finely grated lemon zest or orange zest

instructions: With a rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F. Coat an 8-inch square pan with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.

In a medium bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and ½ teaspoon salt and whisk to incorporate. In a large bowl, combine the sugar and lemon zest and stir until the sugar is moist and fragrant. Add the yogurt, eggs, vanilla, and neutral oil to the sugar and whisk vigorously to blend. Add the flour mixture and, using a flexible spatula, fold to blend the wet and dry ingredients just until no pockets of dry ingredients remain. Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.

Bake the loaf until lightly browned, a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, and the edges begin to pull away from the pan, about 40 minutes. Transfer the pan to a wire rack and let cool to room temperature, about 40 minutes. Turn the bread out of the pan and cut into squares to serve.
noteCook: Salbread can be wrapped tightly in plastic wrap and stored at room temperature for up to 2 days.

recipe.name: Sarth

ingredients.name: LAMB
entries: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds boneless lamb leg, trimmed of fat and cut into 1½-inch pieces

ingredients.name: BEEF

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoons Aleppo pepper or pure Ancho chile powder
{=amount1/c} medium garlic cloves, pressed or grated (about {=amount2/v} teaspoons)

entries: Kosher salt

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds beef sirloin tips, cut into 1½-inch pieces

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} medium red onions, peeled, halved, each half cut into 6 equal chunks

ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons chopped fresh parsley or chives, for garnish

instructions.name: Marinate the lamb:
entries: In a blender, puree the onion, garlic, and ½ cup of water to liquefy. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer, stirring and pressing on the solids to extract as much liquid as possible (you should have about 1 scant cup). Discard or compost the solids. Return the onion juice mixture to the blender, add the olive oil, oregano, cinnamon, 1½ teaspoons salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper and blend to combine. Pour the mixture into a medium nonreactive bowl, add the lamb, and toss to coat. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or up to 24 hours.

instructions.name: Marinate the beef:
entries: In a medium nonreactive bowl, whisk the pomegranate molasses, tomato paste, Aleppo pepper, sumac, allspice, garlic, and 1½ teaspoons salt. Add the beef and toss to coat. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or up to 24 hours.

instructions.name: Prepare and grill the kebabs:
entries: Prepare a medium-hot fire in a charcoal grill or preheat a gas grill on high for 15 minutes. (If using gas, adjust the burners to medium-high and grill with the lid closed.) Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, gently toss the red onions (breaking them up into pieces of two or three layers) with the olive oil and salt and pepper to taste.

instructions: Stand two 10-inch skewers side by side, ½ inch apart, with the pointed sides facing up (see Cook's Note). Thread the set of double skewers with alternating pieces of onion and lamb or beef (about 5 pieces of onion and 5 pieces of meat), making sure that the pieces are not too tight against each other so they can cook evenly. Repeat with the remaining onion, lamb, and beef on the remaining skewers.

Clean and oil the grill grate. Grill the kebabs, turning every 3 minutes, until the onions are tender and charred at the edges and the meat is well browned but still pink inside (medium-rare), 10 to 12 minutes (do not overcook). Remove the kebabs from the grill, rest for about 3 minutes, sprinkle with the parsley or chives, and serve hot.
noteCook: You'll need twelve 10-inch skewers to make the 6 kebabs. Double-skewering helps prevent the pieces of food from spinning as you move the kebabs on the grill.

recipe.name: Scrap And Oil

entries.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoon finely chopped fresh herbs, such as cilantro, mint, or dill

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} pounds vegetables of choice, grated or thinly sliced (see Cook's Note)
{=amount1/v} tablespoons finely chopped fresh herbs, such as cilantro, mint, or dill

ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Olive or vegetable oil, for frying
instructions: In a small bowl, stir together the yogurt, herbs, lemon juice, olive oil, and salt. Cover and set aside in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

In a medium bowl, whisk to combine the chickpea flour, rice flour, and baking powder. In a large bowl, whisk the egg until no streaks remain. Squeeze any excess water out of the wetter vegetables into the sink. To the bowl with the egg, add the vegetables, garlic, chopped herbs, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and pepper. Sprinkle half of the flour mixture onto the vegetable mixture and combine with a rubber spatula. Test the mixture by forming a few patties in your hands. If they fall apart, sprinkle and mix in more of the flour mixture a tablespoon at a time until the patties hold together.

Line a plate with paper towels. In a large skillet, heat ⅛ inch of oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Using a ¼-cup measuring cup, scoop the fritter batter into the pan and gently flatten it with a spatula until it's about ⅓ inch thick. Continue to add batter to the pan, making sure to leave at least 2 inches between the fritters. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the fritters are golden on the bottom, then flip and cook for 2 to 3 more minutes on the second side. Transfer the cooked fritters to the paper towel-lined plate. Continue until no batter remains. Serve at once with the prepared dipping sauce.
noteCook: This recipe is the perfect way to use any leftover vegetables you may have on hand. Ideally, your cut vegetables should all be around the same size. Slice cabbages and onions thinly. Leafy greens like kale or chard work best when blanched, squeezed, and chopped. Grate root vegetables like carrots or sweet potato with the large holes of a box grater. Grate or cut zucchini and other squashes into matchsticks, and make sure to sprinkle them with a few pinches of salt to draw out any moisture. Drain them for at least 30 minutes before patting them dry and adding to your fritter mixture.

recipe.name: Scrimshaw
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes
instructions: In a cocktail shaker, combine the rum, Licor 43, lime juice, coconut cream, and chocolate bitters. Fill it halfway with ice. Cover and shake until well chilled, about 30 seconds. Double strain the mixture to remove any coconut solids before dividing it evenly between two etched-glass coupes. Serve at once.
noteCook: To give this cocktail some additional scrimshaw flair, create a design using cocoa powder and a stencil. Create a stencil by cutting a design from a piece of heavy-weight paper or card stock with a craft knife. Make sure your piece of paper is large enough to rest across the edges of the glass.

recipe.name: Seafoam
ingredients: Roughly cracked or small ice cubes

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} sheet nori, cut into 2 pieces on the bias

instructions.name: To make the nori saline solution:
entries: In a small saucepan, bring the water and salt to a boil over medium-high heat and stir until the salt is completely dissolved. Remove from the heat. Add the nori pieces and stir to submerge. Allow to steep for 30 minutes to an hour. Strain the mixture into a fine-mesh strainer over a cup with a spout to remove the solids and set aside. Store any remaining saline in an airtight jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.

instructions: Fill two highball glasses three-quarters full with ice. Divide the tequila, lime juice, and sparkling water evenly between the two glasses. Add ¼ teaspoon of the nori saline solution to each glass and gently stir to combine. Garnish with a triangle of nori and serve at once.
noteCook: A simple saline solution can bump up the flavors of any cocktail. Omit the nori, store in a bottle with a glass dropper, and keep on hand for whenever you feel like experimenting. A few drops are enough to make a big impact on any drink.

recipe.name: Seared Boar and Potatoes
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoons minced fresh thyme, plus {=amount2/v} extra intact sprigs
{=amount1/v} tablespoons minced fresh rosemary, plus {=amount2/v} extra intact sprigs
{=amount1/v} boneless pork loin roast (about 3 pounds), patted dry with paper towels
{=amount1/v} pounds small Yukon gold potatoes, scrubbed (or peeled if desired), cut into 1½-inch pieces
{=amount1/v} large yellow onions, each cut pole to pole into 6 wedges

instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F.

In a small bowl, combine 1½ teaspoons salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1 tablespoon each minced thyme and rosemary. Tie the pork roast into a neat cylinder with kitchen twine at 1½-inch intervals and sprinkle the salt mixture evenly all over the meat, rubbing it into the surface.
In a large bowl, toss the potatoes and onions with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil to coat. Add ¾ teaspoon each salt and pepper, toss to distribute evenly on the potatoes, and set aside.

In a very large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat, warm the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil until shimmering. Add the pork, fat-side down, adjust the heat to medium, and cook until browned all over, giving it a quarter turn once every 3 minutes (and lowering the heat as necessary if pan drippings threaten to scorch), about 12 minutes total. Transfer the pork to a plate and set aside.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat, pour in the chicken stock, and cook, stirring and scraping the bottom of the skillet to release the caramelized bits, until it's reduced by about half, 3 to 4 minutes. Pour the reduced stock into a small bowl and set aside.

Add the potatoes and onions to the skillet and spread them evenly across the entire surface. Tuck the thyme and rosemary sprigs into the vegetables. Lay the pork, fat side up, on the vegetables. Roast until the center of the meat registers 140°F on an instant-read thermometer, about 60 minutes, turning it over once halfway through that time. Transfer the roast to a carving board (do not turn off the oven), cover it loosely with foil, and rest for 10 to 15 minutes (the internal temperature will increase to about 150°F). Cut off the twine and cut the pork into ½-inch-thick slices.

While the pork rests, adjust the oven temperature to 450°F. Remove the thyme and rosemary sprigs from the vegetables, stir in the garlic and the remaining ½ tablespoon each of the chopped thyme and rosemary, return the skillet to the oven, and continue roasting until the potatoes are golden brown and darker at the edges, about 15 minutes, stirring the vegetables halfway through that time. Taking care with the hot skillet, remove it from the oven, add 1 tablespoon of parsley to the vegetables, and stir to distribute. Spoon the vegetables onto a serving platter, spread them evenly across the surface, arrange the sliced pork over them, and sprinkle the pork lightly with salt and pepper to taste.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add the reserved reduced chicken stock, and bring to a bare simmer, about 90 seconds, stirring and scraping the bottom of the skillet. Pour the warm stock over the sliced pork, sprinkle with the remaining 1 tablespoon of parsley, and serve.
noteCook: You'll need a very large ovenproof skillet, at least 12 inches but preferably 14 inches, to fit the pork and all the potatoes and onions.

The skillet will be screaming hot when it comes out of the oven, though you won't be quite done using it yet. As a visual reminder that it's hot, leave a potholder draped lightly over the end of the handle, well away from the burner.

recipe.name: Seelie Court Cheese and Potato Soup

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} large celery rib, trimmed and chopped
{=amount1/v} pounds russet potatoes, peeled and chopped
{=amount1/xt} 5.2-ounce package Boursin cheese flavored with garlic and fine herbs, crumbled and at room temperature, plus more cheese for garnish (optional)

instructions: In a large saucepan or medium pot over medium-high heat, melt the butter, swirling to coat the pan. Add the onion, celery, bay leaves, and 1 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring until the vegetables are heated through, about 3 minutes. Adjust the heat to medium-low, cover, and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have released their juices, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 40 seconds. Add the chicken broth and potatoes, adjust the heat to medium-high, and bring to a boil. Adjust the heat to low, cover, and simmer until the potatoes are very tender, about 25 minutes. Remove and discard the bay leaves. Add the cheese, cover, and heat until the cheese softens or melts, about 2 minutes.

Remove the soup from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend until smooth. Alternatively, let the soup cool slightly and blend in batches in a countertop blender. Return the soup to the saucepan, if necessary.

Adjust the heat to medium-low, add the half-and-half and 1 teaspoon salt, season with pepper, and warm the soup, stirring occasionally, until heated through, about 4 minutes. Add the parsley and about half the chives and stir to combine. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary. Ladle into individual bowls and sprinkle with additional Boursin (if desired), and the remaining chives before serving.

recipe.name: Sembian Honey-Glazed Rothé Ribs

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} tablespoon neutral-tasting oil, such as vegetable, canola, safflower, or grapeseed
{=amount1/v} to {=amount2/v} pounds baby back ribs, membranes removed, if desired (see Cook's Note)
{=amount1/v} scallions, white and light green parts, thinly sliced, for garnish

instructions: Preheat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the middle of the oven. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack in the sheet.
In a small bowl, whisk together the ketchup, honey, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, and mustard until well-blended. Set aside.

In a nonstick skillet over medium heat, warm the oil until shimmering. Add the onion and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until the onion appears drier, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, and cayenne and cook, stirring constantly until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the ketchup mixture and bring to a simmer, stirring constantly. Continue to simmer, stirring, until the sauce has thickened slightly and the flavors have blended, about 5 minutes. Set aside off the heat to cool briefly; the mixture will thicken as it cools.

Sprinkle both sides of the ribs generously with salt and pepper. Brush about ⅓ cup of the sauce on the bone side, turn the ribs bone-side down, and brush the meaty sides with about ⅔ cup of the remaining sauce. Keeping the ribs bone-side down, roast until the meat is extremely tender (a paring knife should slip easily into the meat) and the meat between the bones in the middle of the racks registers about 205°F on an instant-read thermometer, 2½ to 3 hours; check after 2 hours and cover with foil if the top is getting too dark.

Adjust the oven temperature to 425°F. Brush the remaining ¼ cup sauce on the exposed (meaty) sides of the racks and continue to roast until the sauce heats through but remains sticky, 8 to 10 minutes.
Transfer the ribs to a cutting board and cut as desired. Transfer the cut ribs to a platter, sprinkle with the scallions, and serve hot.
noteCook: On the bone (concave) side of the ribs there is a thin membrane that some people prefer to remove. To do so, slit the corner of the membrane with the tip of a paring knife to loosen it. Grab the loose corner with a paper towel (to improve your grip) and pull it up and off. If it doesn't come off in a single sheet, use the paper-towel trick to help pull off the remaining portion.

recipe.name: Sensate Palate Cleanser

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} medium leek (white and light green parts), chopped

instructions: In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, melt the butter. Add the leek and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until the leek begins to soften, about 2½ minutes. Adjust the heat to medium-low, cover, and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the leek has released its juices, about 5 minutes longer. Remove from the heat and let cool briefly.

Meanwhile, peel one of the cucumbers, leaving about one-fourth of the skin on for a little texture and color. Peel the other two cucumbers completely. Halve all the cucumbers lengthwise and remove the seeds. Finely dice one of the fully peeled halves and set aside. Cut the remaining five halves into roughly 1-inch pieces.

In a blender, combine one-third of the roughly chopped cucumbers, one-third of the leek, and 1 cup of the chicken broth and puree until very smooth, about 40 seconds. Pour the mixture into a large bowl (preferably stainless steel) and set aside. Repeat to blend another third of the cucumbers, leeks, and broth, pouring this batch into the bowl with the first one. For the last batch, combine the remaining roughly chopped cucumber, remaining leeks, and remaining 1 cup chicken broth in the blender; add the half-and-half; and puree. Add to the bowl, stir in the lemon juice and ¾ teaspoon salt, and season with pepper. Stir in the diced cucumber. Cover and refrigerate until cold, about 4 hours.

When ready to serve, stir the soup to blend again, and adjust the seasoning with additional salt and pepper, if necessary. Ladle into individual bowls and garnish each with a sprinkle of pepper and some chives.

recipe.name: Shadowdark
instructions: Using a muddler, pulverize 2 cherries in the bottom of each of two pint glasses. Divide the lager and cider evenly between the two glasses. Top each with 1 ounce of cherry juice. Serve at once.

recipe.name: Silverfruit Pie

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} teaspoons unsalted butter, at room temperature, plus 5 tablespoons melted and still warm
{=amount1/v} whole graham crackers, broken into rough pieces
{=amount1/xt} 20-ounce can lychees (peeled, pitted, and in heavy syrup)
{=amount1/v} ounces mascarpone, at cool room temperature

instructions: With a rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 9-inch pie plate with the room-temperature butter, and set aside.

In a food processor, process the graham crackers to fine crumbs, about 20 seconds. Add the brown sugar and 1 pinch salt and pulse to combine. With the motor running, slowly add the melted butter through the feed tube and process until the mixture resembles wet sand, about 20 seconds. Pour the mixture into the pie plate and press into an even, compact layer across the bottom and up the sides. Wipe out the food processor work bowl to use again.

Bake the crust until lightly browned and fragrant, about 12 minutes, rotating the pie plate about halfway through. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool to room temperature (the crust will firm up as it cools).

Meanwhile, drain the lychees well and blot them dry with paper towel. Line a plate or baking sheet with paper towels in a double layer. Cut each lychee in half, place them cut sides down on the paper towel-lined plate, and refrigerate until needed, at least 1 hour.

Add the mascarpone, confectioners' sugar, rosewater, vanilla, and ¼ teaspoon salt to the food processor and pulse until combined and smooth, stopping once or twice to scrape down the work bowl, about 10 two-second pulses. Scrape the mixture into the crust, gently spread it in an even layer, and refrigerate until firmer, at least 1 hour. Arrange the lychees, cut-sides down, over the mascarpone, covering the entire surface, and gently press them into the mixture to anchor.

In a small saucepan over medium heat, warm the apple jelly until warm to the touch and beginning to become fluid, stirring to smooth out any lumps. Off heat, cool the fluid jelly for about 5 minutes. Stir it again and, using a pastry brush, gently dab and brush the jelly over the lychees. Refrigerate for 30 minutes, sprinkle the lemon zest over the pie, and serve immediately.
noteCook: Rather than warming the apple jelly on the stovetop, you can warm it in a microwave-safe container in the microwave, using partial power, for about 30 seconds, stopping to check and stir it about every 10 seconds.

Even though you drain and dry the lychees, they'll retain enough moisture to weep on the pie if they sit for too long. It's best to serve the pie no more than an hour after glazing it. If you have leftovers, refrigerate them and expect the jam to slide off the lychees and pool between them and at the edges of the crust. If you'd like, use a small bit of paper towel to blot away visible liquid before serving.

recipe.name: Skyway Special

ingredients.entry: {=amount1/v} cup cake or all-purpose flour (see Cook's Notes)

ingredients: Pinch of cream of tartar (optional; see Cook's Notes)
instructions: Separate the eggs, placing both the yolks and the whites into large bowls. Put the bowl of whites into the freezer while working with the yolks, about 5 minutes.

Add the milk and vanilla to the yolks and whisk until thoroughly combined and uniform. Sift the flour, baking powder, and salt into the yolk mixture, stir until thoroughly combined (do not overmix), and set aside.
Set two large, deep nonstick or well-seasoned cast-iron or carbon steel skillets (with tight-fitting lids) over low heat while working with the egg whites (see Cook's Notes).

With a handheld electric mixer or a stand mixer fitted with the whisk, beat the whites on medium-low speed until frothy. Add the cream of tartar, if using; adjust the speed to medium-high, and continue beating; gradually add the sugar, until the whites are very thick, glossy, and they hold stiff peaks when you pull out the beater, at least 1½ minutes. (Take care not to overwhip the whites—they'd start to look a bit chunky and dull—which makes them more prone to deflate.) Add one-quarter of the beaten whites to the yolk mixture and stir until uniform. Add half of the remaining beaten whites, and with a large flexible spatula, rapidly and gently fold them into the mixture. Add the remaining beaten whites and repeat to fold them into the mixture until just combined and homogenous (do not overmix).

Adjust the heat under the skillets to medium-low. Pour about 2½ teaspoons of oil into each skillet, brush it evenly over the entire cooking surface, and with a folded paper towel, lightly dab away any visible oil to create a bare, even film. Using a portion scoop, dipper, or large spoon, gently place as many roughly 2½-tablespoon portions of batter as will fit comfortably into each skillet, leaving at least an inch of space between them. Top each portion with a second portion of the same size, making a tall mound of each. To each skillet add about 1 tablespoon of water, dividing it among three empty spots (taking care that no water touches any of the pancakes). Cover the skillets and cook for 2 minutes.

Remove the lids and add a third scoop of batter onto each mound. To each skillet add another tablespoon of water in the same manner as before, replace the lids, and continue cooking until the pancakes are set and the bottoms are golden brown, 4 to 6 minutes.

Using a heat-safe spatula, carefully flip the pancakes. Add another tablespoon of water to each skillet in the same manner as before, replace the lids, and continue cooking until the bottoms are golden brown and the sides appear dry and set, about 4 minutes.

Transfer the pancakes to a large plate or tray, dust them liberally with confectioners' sugar, and serve immediately with whipped cream (if using). Meanwhile, repeat the cooking process with any remaining batter.
noteCook: If you cook your batter in two batches in a single skillet (rather than in two skillets), the pancakes from the second batch won't be as fluffy.
